chapters.title: Chapter 2151: Changes.
paragraphs: "So that’s what happened..."
Nux spoke as the marks that appeared on his body disappeared and he was done reading the woman’s body.
"Looks quite useful."
Amaya commented.
Nux had already shared the vision with all his wives, so all of them were currently on the same page.
"Mhm."
Aeliana nodded as well.
"It is basically the fastest way to capture anyone without having to worry about any reinforcements."
Thyra added. The assassin was impressed. Her mind could come up with countless scenarios where this would be useful.

The vision they saw was similar to what Faustina described. The woman first noticed Nux standing behind her; at first, she didn’t think too much—her mind had countless things to worry about, she barely noticed anyone around her, all her attention was on Carlen and how to get her world out of the trouble it was in.
However, after Carlen sent her away and Nux attacked him a few minutes later, everything changed.
First, Nux killed Carlen, shocking her and every single being present around her. Then Lord Silvaris arrived; the woman too, was engulfed into Silvaris’s Domain, so she saw the ’fight’ clearly.
Finally, once Silvaris was defeated and the woman saw fourteen Eternal Level beings surrounding him, she thought Nux would finally face the consequences of his actions but...
But then the air around him trembled, and just like that—everyone, Nux, Eternals, Sharnoth who was with Nux, and unconscious Silvaris who was in her arms—everyone disappeared.

For a few seconds, everyone was utterly confused; their minds were frozen, unable to even process what had happened, and only when Gracevale and the Universe trembled did they finally come back to their senses.
Yes, to an outsider, it was all a blur.
The moment Nux activated his Domain, they were no longer in Gracevale.
And if this could be used well...
Nux grinned at that possibility.
"What about the Supreme Worlds? How did they react?"
Suddenly, Astaria questioned.
Even though Nux had returned and was safe, she still wanted to know how the Supreme Worlds were going to act.
"Mother says that there are around fifty Light Borns in Gracevale right now."
Nux answered.
Since Azriel was still there, hiding using the Universe’s power, there was no way the Supreme Borns—even if they were all Eternals—would be able to find him.
"Did they find anything?"
Astaria questioned, and with a big wide grin on his face—
"No.
There is no connection to the place my Domain takes me to and where the Domain was created."
"So basically... they have no way to come find you once you activate your Domain?"
Rune questioned as she blinked repeatedly; she was having a hard time believing just how... broken this ability was.
And Nux—
"Yes."
He nodded, the grin on his face never fading away.
After all, now that what he was thinking was proven to be true, then—
"The Supreme Worlds have a big headache coming."
Felberta commented. She knew exactly what this man was planning to do when she saw the grin on his face.
Honestly, at this point, she somewhat pitied the Supreme Worlds for having to go against him.
But of course—𝒇𝒓𝒆𝒆𝙬𝒆𝒃𝓷𝒐𝓿𝙚𝙡.𝒄𝓸𝒎
"When are you going to move?"
Eldraeth questioned with a grin. She too was looking forward to the Chaos that was about to ensue.
Nux laughed when he saw her face and then—
"Right now."
He answered.
"And what about her? What do we do with her?"
Melia questioned as she pointed at the woman she was holding.
Nux stared at her for a moment and then—
"I’ll take her back to her world first."
"She will become their target."
Riona commented.
She could easily see the Supreme Worlds, especially the Supreme World of Light, going after her to try and learn something about them.
"I do not think they will have time for them."
Nux, however, shook his head.
"And if they do...?"
Evane questioned, a little worried. After all, the woman was completely innocent; if anything, she was a victim.
"There is nothing we can do to help her."
Nux shook his head.

"If we let her go, she will be targeted; if we keep her here, her disappearance would make her entire world a target. Having read her memories, that is the last thing she would want. She would rather be the target herself than let her world be affected by it."
"Can we... really not do anything?"
The Elf questioned in a low voice.
Yes, by now, they had killed countless, and yes, many affected by their actions were innocent but...
It still wasn’t a feeling she could get used to.
Nux turned silent, not knowing what to say.

Even he could see that his actions had entered a gray area. At this point, the number of deaths he was responsible for was easily hundreds of billions. Heck, literal worlds had faced mass deaths because they couldn’t defend themselves from the Universe’s Rage—and while those deaths were the Universe’s fault, in the end, Nux’s actions were the trigger for what happened.

Nux was everything, but he wasn’t hypocrite enough to believe he was innocent or virtuous. The only thing he could say to convince himself was that he did what he did to ensure his and his wives’ safety.
But as he now stood in front of his worried wife... he just... he couldn’t say anything that could possibly comfort her.

After all, he truly could not help this woman and her world—not when helping them would mean risking his and his wives’ lives and standing in front of the Supreme Worlds without any trickery, something Nux had no plans to do.
Yes, in this situation, even Nux was helpless. This woman was going to be one of the countless victims he had.
Or at least...
That was what Nux initially thought but then—
"...there is something we can do."
Shadow spoke up, staring at Nux as she thought of something they had never done before.
"What do you mean?"
Nux tilted his head, a bit confused. Soon, however, his expression changed as he realized what the woman was hinting at.
"Are you telling me to devour her World?"
"The Universe is now complete; we can easily support a World and all the life in it."
Shadow answered.
Amaya, however, frowned at those words.
"There must be hundreds of millions of people in her world; we do not have enough ’space’ to devour them all."
She countered.
"We do not need ’spaces’ to devour beings anymore.

The ’spaces’ were needed before because our Universe was not complete—entities from another Universe could not survive in here, so the ’spaces’ were needed so that Nux could make some entities a part of him, a part of his Universe.
However, now that our Universe is complete, entities from different Universes can now survive inside.
So as long as Nux doesn’t wish to devour their abilities, bloodlines, Laws, or any other power,
He no longer needs to use ’space’ to devour people.
He can now devour a functioning World and make it a part of his Universe, together with the beings of that particular world."
Shadow explained in an oddly mature tone—a tone that the other women had a difficult time adjusting to, especially since it came from her.
But then, as if all this was an illusion, the woman shrugged and—
"Of course, all of this is still a theory.
Who knows, we might even kill all people of her world if we devour them."
She laughed irresponsibly.

chapters.title: Chapter 2152: The Light Borns.
paragraphs: RUMBLE RUMBLE RUMBLE
THUNDER THUNDER THUNDER
Gracevale trembled in fear as it sensed its connection with its Eternals disappear out of nowhere.
And it wasn’t just Gracevale itself,
RUMBLE RUMBLE RUMBLE
THUNDER THUNDER THUNDER
The very Universe trembled, and unlike Gracevale, which felt fear, the Universe was enraged.
It happened again, and this time, on a much larger scale.
Fifteen Eternals!
It lost fifteen Eternals!
The Universe was throwing a fit, its trembling destroyed thousands of Lowest Level Worlds.
Anomaly—the Universe wanted to do whatever it took to get rid of that entity!
And it wasn’t just the Universe that wanted that; the Supreme World of Light was the same.
Gracevale’s once bright and peaceful sky suddenly began pulsing with a bright, golden light, making every being raise their head and look at what was happening.
The clouds split open, and beams of pure, beautiful energy descended, and in an instant, every being in Gracevale dropped to their knees.
After all, they knew what this light meant.
The Light Borns had arrived.
What’s even more shocking was that there wasn’t just one or two—
There were a total of forty of them.

Each one shone like a miniature sun, their wings bright enough to light the world below. They wore long, white-golden robes engraved with runes that felt otherworldly. Their presence alone cleansed the air.
"It’s them... the Supreme World of Light sent the Light Borns..."
Voices of citizens filled the air, trembling between awe and... relief.
"They must’ve come to investigate the disappearance of Lord Silvaris and others!"
"Yes! Whoever that man was! He will now face the consequences of his bold action!"
"Gracevale will be safe now!"
The talks began.

These people had just witnessed Lord Silvaris, a being they considered to be one of the strongest and their protector, defeated within a matter of seconds. The sudden disappearance of the unknown enemy and all other Eternals only surprised them even further.
And when the Universe and Gracevale reacted, this surprise turned into fear.
These people had never once experienced an otherworldly enemy’s attack in the first place, not to mention one at such a grand scale.
What would happen now?
Where had the Eternals disappeared to?
Why was Gracevale acting like this?𝑓𝘳𝑒𝑒𝓌𝘦𝘣𝘯ℴ𝑣𝘦𝑙.𝘤𝑜𝑚
What was going to happen next?
What was going to happen to... them?
And what if... now that the Eternals weren’t here to protect them, another enemy from a different faction attacked?
All these questions appeared in their heads. They were scared—it was natural for it to happen, especially when their very world was trembling and screaming in fear and panic.
The Light Borns’ entry, however, calmed them.
After all, their presence meant the direct involvement of the Supreme World of Light—no one was going to act against them now, not even enemies from another faction.
Yes, the Light Borns’ mere presence filled the people with hope.
But...
The Light Borns didn’t speak to the people.
Their glowing eyes swept across the land, across the ruined plaza where the Gracevale Eternals had disappeared.
At the center of their group stood their leader—Serion, one of the oldest among the Light Borns.
His wings were vast and golden like crystal fire, his voice carried a strange calming power.
"Spread out,"
He ordered in an emotionless voice.
"Read every memory, every echo.
Leave no place untouched."
At his command, the other thirty-nine vanished, turning into streaks of golden light that shot across Gracevale.
The citizens stared in awe as the Light Borns appeared in front of them. Soon, however, their awe turned into panic as the Light Borns extended their hands and grabbed their foreheads.
It was clear what they were doing.
However...
The people of Gracevale did not mind.
"I... I saw him!"
A female Auriel shouted as she saw a Light Born standing about a hundred meters away from her.
"He was an Incubus! A very handsome Incubus! He stood there and smiled—and then they vanished! All of them! I also felt that the sky turned dark, but it didn’t!"
She told everything without being asked.
Her face seemed flushed, almost as if she was possessed.

The Light Born, hearing her words, frowned. He vanished and appeared in front of her. The woman’s smile widened even further—this was the first time she was seeing a Light Born; being blessed with such luck...
She was so content that even if she died right now, she would not complain.
Of course, the Light Born did not care about what she was thinking. He simply grabbed her head, making the woman tremble with even more joy, and just like that, he began reading her memories.
When he got what he wanted, he waved his hand, and suddenly, a projection appeared in the air, showing Nux surrounded by fourteen Eternals—all from the woman’s perspective.

At the same time, the rest of the Light Borns had found witnesses as well, and every one of them started adding into the projection the first Light Born had created, adding different perspectives to it.
Within just a minute of arriving, the Light Borns had managed to create a perfect, three-dimensional projection in the air, showing exactly what happened and how it ended.
With that projection, even the people who did not know what happened and who was responsible for it now knew Nux’s face.
Serion, who hadn’t moved from his place, narrowed his eyes as he saw Nux. Suddenly, one of the Light Borns appeared beside him and—
"He erased the trace of his arrival,"
He spoke quietly.
"Completely."
He didn’t act excessively respectful—even if Serion was older than him and maybe a little stronger, in the end, they were both Eternals with similar bloodlines.
Another Light Born arrived a second later and—
"The people’s memories are consistent. They weren’t manipulated either; there wasn’t enough time."
Serion frowned. Just... how did he completely eraseallthe traces? That too, in such a short time?
There had to be something, no?
A single clue—
And just then,
"One woman is missing."
Another Light Born reported.
Serion’s expression changed. He quickly glanced at the Light Born and—
"Wh—"
However, before he could complete his question—
RUMBLE RUMBLE RUMBLE
THUNDER THUNDER THUNDER
The Universe reacted again.

chapters.title: Chapter 2153: No leads.
paragraphs: "One woman is missing."
Serion’s expression changed at that report; he turned towards the being who reported, wanting to ask more,
"Wh—"
However, before he could complete his question—
RUMBLE RUMBLE RUMBLE
THUNDER THUNDER THUNDER
Their surroundings shook again.
It started with the skies roaring in anger, almost as if they would fall apart. For a moment, the people frowned, confused as to what happened, but then,
The ground shook with a rumble, as if it was about to crack open.
An effect that every single one of them felt.
The Light Borns froze and stared at each other in shock; even Serion was no exception.
"Again...?"
One of them narrowed their eyes, finally breaking their silence.

Serion spread his wings wide in silence, balancing his body as the world around him trembled. Unlike others, he didn’t react as strongly; his mind had already started speculating different reasons as to why it was happening.
"The Universe! It is reacting again!"
"Again!? What is happening!?"
"This is—"

As panic began to spread and the rest of the people began to realize what was happening, one hundred and twenty-one radiant ’Divine Towers’ that were spread all over Gracevale swayed gently, and enormous golden sigils buried across the city lit up one by one.
The ground beneath every building began to glow with sacred runes. Massive pillars of light shot upward, connecting sky and earth.
The defensive Artifacts of Gracevale—the creations given directly by the Supreme World of Light—had awakened on their own and, in an instant—
WHOOOOOOM𝚏𝗿𝗲𝐞𝚠𝕖𝐛𝗻𝗼𝐯𝕖𝚕.𝚌𝗼𝗺
From every corner of the world, waves of holy energy erupted, turning into a silent, suppressing wave that spread all over Gracevale, and—
The trembling stopped instantly, and the rumbling skies turned silent.

Even though the Universe outside was still trembling in anger, Gracevale, in less than a second, had calmed down to the point that people who weren’t sensitive enough wouldn’t even realize that something had happened.

Of course, this wasn’t the first time it had happened; the Universe had reacted many times in the past few years, and the defensive system had activated every single time. The people had pretty much gotten used to this sight.
But not today.
Today, the Universe’s reaction had an effect on Gracevale.
The entire place, especially the Hall where the Light Borns were gathered, was deathly silent.
The people looked up, trembling, still kneeling on the ground. The Light Borns landed one by one, their wings folding softly.
And with a grim look on his face, Serion turned towards one of the Light Borns standing beside him and—
"Find out what happened."
The other Light Born didn’t waste time responding either; he quickly took out the artifact he used to contact his subordinates and asked for a report.
Within three seconds, the answer came.
An answer that lightened the Light Born’s heavy expression.
"A Lowest Level World named Greenmarch has disappeared. It is not a big deal."
He reported.

While someone at their level knew how the disappearance of a World—no matter what level—decreased the total amount of Energy in the Universe and ultimately weakened it, in the end, it was the Universe’s problem, not theirs.

If anything, more than thinking about how the Universe was affected by it, the Light Borns were angered by the fact that while they were investigating the enemy here, he was targeting some other world far away that had nothing to do with it.
It was clear that the enemy was trying to mock them, and the Light Borns, who had never once felt that way in their long lives—they were enraged.
Of course, not every Light Born thought the same, especially when one of them heard the name of the World that was devoured.
"Greenmarch?"
He asked.
Everyone turned towards him, and the Light Born who gathered the information nodded,
"Yes, it is a Lowest Level World in the Fercry Sector."
Seeing the Light Born’s expression, Serion frowned.
"Do you know about this world?"
He asked a strange question. How could a Light Born know about a mere Lowest Level World? Even his subordinates wouldn’t look into such worlds.
But shockingly—
The Light Born nodded.
"The missing woman I mentioned before—"
He began. Serion nodded, remembering their conversation that happened just before the rumbling began,
"She comes from Greenmarch."
He reported with a grim look on his face, and the rest of the Light Borns had the same expression as him.
"Are you saying that the only lead we had is now gone...?"
Serion questioned with a solemn look on his face, and the Light Born nodded, the grim look on his face not fading away.
"Do we have any other leads?"
Serion questioned as he looked around, but...
No one said anything.
"I had planned to find the woman or investigate the world she came from."
The Light Born shook his head.
"What if we investigate the worlds Greenmarch had relationships with? It doesn’t matter how strong or weak the relationship is; I am sure we will get something out of it."
Another Light Born raised her voice, suggesting a way forward.
Serion looked at her and—
"I will leave that to you. I need an answer within an hour."
The woman nodded and disappeared without saying anything.
Serion then turned towards the rest,
"Anything else?"
He questioned, wanting a solution to the problem.
"I will investigate all of them again."
One suggested.

Serion nodded, giving permission. A few more suggested other things, and Serion permitted them all. He knew every single one of them was capable; as long as there was even the slightest lead, they would follow it till they got to the very end of it and got something out of it.
Just that...
They couldn’t find anything.
Even after half an hour had passed, no one found anything. The enemy had left no trace at all; it felt like they were looking for an enemy that did not exist.
And the worst part?
Bzzz Bzzz Bzzz
The Supreme World of Light was now contacting Serion—
The Light Infinity wanted to know what he found.

chapters.title: Chapter 2154: Just… what happened…?
paragraphs: A being with pale ivory skin with green-gold undertones, long, moss-green hair, pointed ears, and golden-green armor slowly regained his consciousness and opened his eyes.
The first thing he felt was the scent of grass.
Fresh, damp, and warm—the kind only his world could carry. As his vision slowly cleared, the soft gold of Greenmarch’s eternal dawn greeted him.
He was lying on a wide meadow—a sea of emerald blades that glowed faintly under sunlight.
Everything looked exactly like it was supposed to, like it used to, but...
But something felt different...
His surroundings felt... heavier and... dimmer.
The sky, normally bright with two silver suns and rivers of light running through the clouds, now looked pale and bruised.

The being pushed himself up with a grunt. His long green hair was messy and tangled. His golden armor, engraved with flowing leaf patterns, was cracked in several places. His own greenish and faintly luminous blood stained his chestplate.
With a hazy mind, he looked around, and the instant he did, he froze.
Tens of thousands of his soldiers were scattered across the field—all unconscious, some were breathing heavily, while some were... unnervingly still.
"What...?"
The being let out a soft, confused, and grim voice.
The being was Ravana Greenmarch, the Progenitor of Verdans, the race that lived in the Lowest Level World called Greenmarch.
The confused Ravana slowly took a step forward, his heavy shoes stepping on the grass in front of him.
Whoom
The land responded faintly.
The ground pulsed once, as if recognizing its master. Ravana also sensed his link with Greenmarch’s Will, but he very quickly noticed something.
The link... it was much weaker than before; he could barely sense it.
Ravana’s face turned even grimmer.
Something had happened.
However, Ravana knew he couldn’t lose his calm, not at a time like this. Slowly, he started looking around.
This place he was in, he recognized it.

It was the Fields of Aurellion, the open plain that spread from the heart of Greenmarch’s capital to the forests beyond. He turned to the east and saw the Verdant Pillars—tall living trees that twisted together into shimmering towers of green light.
Trees that were supposed to glow endlessly, but...
But today, their light was flickering.
Farther away, the Great Bloom, a massive floating flower-city, hung low in the sky. The city itself was in complete shambles; almost no building was in one piece, everything was destroyed.
A sight Ravana had already gotten used to. He knew Greenmarch’s condition wasn’t stable, especially because of the constant Universal Tremors, but today, everything looked even grimmer.
"Just... what happened...?"
He muttered with a frown, his hand gripping his head as he began recalling everything he remembered to connect the events.

He remembered ordering his men to create temporary stays for half of their people who had lost their homes, but then suddenly, Greenmarch’s Will roared through his mind, warning him of an unknown entity that had appeared out of nowhere.
What was surprising was that unlike in cases of usual otherworldly intruders, where Greenmarch’s Will knew about them the moment they entered Greenmarch, this was... different.
The unknown entity had already entered Greenmarch, and Greenmarch was only able to sense it when it released its energy.
It made its presence known by itself, and if it hadn’t... Greenmarch would have never known.
Of course, at the time, Ravana didn’t care about these details. His World’s Will informed him of the intruder—it was his duty to go and deal with it.
And that’s what he did. Gathering his men, he moved, instantly arriving in these fields—the place where Greenmarch had sensed the foreign energy.
Then...
Ravana frowned, trying to recall further memories; his memories, however, started becoming hazy.
He remembered standing on the same ground, facing a silhouette—he didn’t remember the face or even the shape.
Just the... strange calm around him seemed... overwhelming—especially considering that the being wasthiscalm when he was hovering in front of more than forty thousand soldiers.
Ravana remembered trying to speak, to ask who the being was and what he wanted, but then—
But then the intruder maybe released his Aura and—
Nothingness.
Ravana couldn’t even recall the strike, the sound, or the energy.
It was as if reality itself bent inward, forcing everything into silence, and the next thing he knew, he was here.
No matter what else Ravana tried to recall, his mind was completely blank.
It was clear,

They were all knocked unconscious even before they could do anything. Even his cracked armor and the blood on it—it wasn’t because of battle; it was because his armor and his body couldn’t take on the pressure and cracked—just like his mind.
Ravana gulped, and a grim look appeared on his face.

Ravana wasn’t an arrogant fool like most Progenitors who were the strongest in their worlds. Ravana knew his place. He knew that in the vast Universe, there were countless beings who could destroy him, his army, and his world—all on their own with a mere swing of their arms.
But...
What Ravana couldn’t understand was...
What exactly happened?
They were attacked, but he could sense that none of his men were killed; his world wasn’t devoured either.
So what exactly did that foreign entity do?
Also, why had his connection with Greenmarch weakened to such a degree?
"So you are finally awake."
Suddenly, Ravana heard a voice.
He turned, and his eyes fell on an unreasonably beautiful woman standing in front of him.
"Who are you?"
Ravana asked, and for a moment, the woman didn’t say anything.
"Right...
I didn’t come up with a way to introduce myself."
She admitted honestly, and Ravana...
He had no idea what he was supposed to say here.
He waited for the woman, who seemed to be thinking about something, to explain everything, and finally—
"You can think of me like the Universe’s Will.
Yes, I am this Universe’s Will."
The woman answered.
"What...?"
Ravana blinked, unable to believe what he was hearing.
"The Universe’s Will...?"
"Mhm."
"...and you want me to believe that?"
Ravana questioned honestly.𝕗𝐫𝐞𝕖𝕨𝐞𝗯𝚗𝕠𝘃𝐞𝚕.𝐜𝗼𝚖
Shadow stared at him for a moment, then she sighed, and with a wave of her hand, Ravana’s daughter appeared around her.
"Does that hel—"
"Riana!!"
Ravana, not listening to Shadow’s words, quickly rushed and grabbed his daughter, now glaring at Shadow in anger.
And Shadow...
"Right,
Bringing out your daughter like that wasn’t the best move either—just what is happening to me? Why am I not thinking things through?"
Shadow muttered to herself again, still quite unbothered by the angry man in front of her.

chapters.title: Chapter 2155: So… are you going to make us all… disappear?
paragraphs: "Right,
Bringing out your daughter like that wasn’t the best move either—just what is happening to me?
Why am I not thinking things through?"
Shadow tilted her head, confused by her own actions, completely ignoring the angry man glaring at her as if he was going to murder her.

After all, the man posed absolutely no threat to her; after all, he was merely a Sovereign, that too, now inside Nux’s Universe where Shadow had absolute strength. Ravana wouldn’t be able to hurt Shadow even if he had billions of lives.
Shadow quickly shook her head and continued what she came here for—
"So, as I was saying..."

She began her story, and this time, Ravana listened. As wary as he was, he could tell something was wrong, and this odd, unknown woman seemed to have answers. Plus, his daughter was already safe in his hands, so while the situation might still be dangerous, Ravana didn’t feel like the woman in front of him was an enemy.
"You remember how the Universe trembled a few minutes before that unknown entity appeared in your world, correct?"
Shadow began with a question.
Ravana nodded with a grim look on his face; that tremor had destroyed his world even further, so he obviously did not forget about it.
"That happened because Gracevale was attacked."
Shadow revealed, and Ravana...
"What...?"
He widened his eyes in disbelief.
Gracevale was a High-Level World that had deep connections with the Supreme World of Light—who in their right min—
"Yes, yes, keep all the disbelief to yourself."
Shadow interrupted Ravana’s line of thought as she waved her hand in a dismissive manner. She had no intention of wasting her time here.

"All you need to know is that Gracevale was attacked. All their Progenitors, who came to face the enemy, disappeared. The Supreme World of Light sent Light Borns to investigate, but the enemy left no trace.
The only problem was..."
Shadow stared at the woman in Ravana’s arms and...
"Along with fifteen Progenitors, one woman, otherwise insignificant and unrelated to the situation, had disappeared as well.

That woman was taken by the enemy, just like he took away the Progenitors, but the Light Borns misunderstood the situation and suspected the woman to be the enemy’s ally—hence, an enemy that needs to be found."
"Why are you telling me all that...?"
Ravana asked directly, confused.

The news of Gracevale being attacked already surprised him. Adding to that, the woman continued giving more information without letting him absorb what was already said. His mind felt overwhelmed, not to mention Ravana did not like how the woman was staring at his daughter.
Something... something felt ominous.
And it was.
"The woman who disappeared is your daughter."
Shadow revealed, and in an instant, Ravana’s expression changed.
"My daughter had... disappeared...?"
He asked in disbelief.
"Yes."
Shadow nodded.
"So the people from the Supreme World of Light think she is an enemy...?"
He asked another question, and once again, Shadow nodded, and Ravana panicked.
"No! We have to make things clear!
My daughter is not an enemy! How can she be the enemy of a Supreme World!? She is not even a Sovereign yet!
I-I need to talk to them! I n-need to tell them that my daughter was taken by the enem—"
Suddenly, Ravana froze as something clicked in his head.
He turned his head towards Shadow in an almost mechanical manner, then, with his face now paler than before—
"Y-You said that my daughter was taken away by the enemy... then why do you..."
He couldn’t even complete his question.
Shadow, however, understood what he wanted to say and nodded again.
"Yes, we were the ones who attacked Gracevale."
"What...?"
"Well, technically, he is my husband who loves me the most, but same thing."
Shadow shrugged casually.
And obviously, Ravana was not on the same page of humor as her. He stared at Shadow, frozen in fear.
Seeing that, Shadow sighed.
"Come on, use your head a little, will you?"
She began.
"If we wanted to kill you, you or your daughter wouldn’t be standing here. All these soldiers around you wouldn’t be alive either."
"...then what do you want from us?"
Ravana asked in a low, fearful voice.
If this woman was someone who attacked Gracevale and escaped, then... he obviously stood no chance against her.
"Well, nothing really. You are just here because we wanted to protect you and the people of your world."
"...what?"
Ravana blinked.
How was kidnapping his daughter and involving her in a situation as dangerous as this protecting them in any way?
He wanted to ask this out loud, but he didn’t dare to.
Shadow obviously knew what he was thinking, and she just nodded,
"I have read your and your daughter’s memories; you people are not fools.

You do not foolishly believe that the Supreme World of Light is what they pretend to be. They are no different from other Supreme Worlds. To them, you and your people are just pawns they can use and discard anytime they desire.
But this incident made a link between the enemy the Supreme World of Light desperately wants to catch and your daughter.
Even if the link is weak, since it is the only thing they have, they will investigate it thoroughly.

First, they will target your daughter, then it will be you, then your entire world. Even if they do not find anything, they will eradicate you and your people just to ensure the enemy isn’t working with you.
There is no situation where you get out of this unless..."
"Unless...?"
Ravana gulped.
"Unless you disappear from the Universe."
"...disappear from the... Universe?"
Ravana blinked, confused by those words.
Was this woman... trying to kill them?
No, that made no sense.
It was something else.
Ravana thought about it for a while, and soon, he connected those words with something Shadow said before...
"By disappearing...𝑓𝘳𝑒𝑒𝓌𝘦𝘣𝘯ℴ𝑣𝘦𝑙.𝘤𝑜𝑚
Is this similar to how the Gracevale Progenitors disappeared...?"
He asked carefully, and Shadow raised her eyebrow, impressed.
From Ravana’s memories, she knew he was a sharp man, but she didn’t expect him to make the connection, especially considering his current mental state.
"Yes, you can think of it like that."
"So... are you going to make us all... disappear? What will happen to us when you do...?"
The Greenmarch Progenitor questioned, and Shadow...
"You have already disappeared."
She just smiled.

Something... something felt ominous.
And it was.
"The woman who disappeared is your daughter."
Shadow revealed, and in an instant, Ravana’s expression changed.
"My daughter had... disappeared...?"
He asked in disbelief.
"Yes."
Shadow nodded.
"So the people from the Supreme World of Light think she is an enemy...?"
He asked another question, and once again, Shadow nodded, and Ravana panicked.
"No!
We have to make things clear!
My daughter is not an enemy!
How can she be the enemy of a Supreme World!?
She is not even a Sovereign yet!
I-I need to talk to them!
I n-need to tell them that my daughter was taken by the enem—"
Suddenly, Ravana froze as something clicked in his head.
He turned his head towards Shadow in an almost mechanical manner, then, with his face now paler than before—
"Y-You said that my daughter was taken away by the enemy... then why do you..."
He couldn’t even complete his question.
Shadow, however, understood what he wanted to say and nodded again.
"Yes, we were the ones who attacked Gracevale."
"What...?"
"Well, technically, he is my husband who loves me the most, but same thing."
Shadow shrugged casually.
And obviously, Ravana was not on the same page of humor as her.
He stared at Shadow, frozen in fear.
Seeing that, Shadow sighed.
"Come on, use your head a little, will you?"
She began.
"If we wanted to kill you, you or your daughter wouldn’t be standing here.
All these soldiers around you wouldn’t be alive either."
"...then what do you want from us?"
Ravana asked in a low, fearful voice.
If this woman was someone who attacked Gracevale and escaped, then... he obviously stood no chance against her.
"Well, nothing really.
You are just here because we wanted to protect you and the people of your world."
"...what?"
Ravana blinked.
How was kidnapping his daughter and involving her in a situation as dangerous as this protecting them in any way?
He wanted to ask this out loud, but he didn’t dare to.
Shadow obviously knew what he was thinking, and she just nodded,
"I have read your and your daughter’s memories; you people are not fools.
You do not foolishly believe that the Supreme World of Light is what they pretend to be.
They are no different from other Supreme Worlds.
To them, you and your people are just pawns they can use and discard anytime they desire.
But this incident made a link between the enemy the Supreme World of Light desperately wants to catch and your daughter.
Even if the link is weak, since it is the only thing they have, they will investigate it thoroughly.
First, they will target your daughter, then it will be you, then your entire world.
Even if they do not find anything, they will eradicate you and your people just to ensure the enemy isn’t working with you.
There is no situation where you get out of this unless..."
"Unless...?"
Ravana gulped.
"Unless you disappear from the Universe."
"...disappear from the...
Universe?"
Ravana blinked, confused by those words.
Was this woman... trying to kill them?
No, that made no sense.
It was something else.
Ravana thought about it for a while, and soon, he connected those words with something Shadow said before...
"By disappearing...𝑓𝘳𝑒𝑒𝓌𝘦𝘣𝘯ℴ𝑣𝘦𝑙.𝘤𝑜𝑚
Is this similar to how the Gracevale Progenitors disappeared...?"
He asked carefully, and Shadow raised her eyebrow, impressed.
From Ravana’s memories, she knew he was a sharp man, but she didn’t expect him to make the connection, especially considering his current mental state.
"Yes, you can think of it like that."
"So... are you going to make us all... disappear?
What will happen to us when you do...?"
The Greenmarch Progenitor questioned, and Shadow...
"You have already disappeared."
She just smiled.

chapters.title: Chapter 2156: I… I don’t think I can help you.
paragraphs: "So... are you going to make us all... disappear? What will happen to us when you do...?"
The Greenmarch Progenitor questioned, his voice cracking in uncertainty and fear.
And Shadow—
"You have already disappeared."
She just smiled, instantly defusing all the thoughts inside Ravana’s head.
"What...?"
The Greenmarch Progenitor did not know how to react.
Shadow understood that, so in order to skip some explanations, she waved her hand and suddenly, fourteen beings that Ravana recognized instantly appeared in front of her.
"Y-You... all of you..."
He stuttered.
Unable to believe that the fourteen Eternals who had supposedly ’disappeared’ were now standing right in front of him—all with their heads bowed. A scene he never once thought he would get to see.
After all, even though he was a Progenitor, in the end, he came from a lowest-level world. To be able to see leaders of one of the strongest high-level worlds lowering their heads in such a manner...
Slowly, he turned back towards the woman he was talking to—
In an instant, the way he looked at her changed. After all, the man knew that he wasn’t the one these fourteen monstrous beings were bowing to.
And Shadow used this chance.
"You, your people, along with your entire world, have already disappeared from the universe, just like them."
She informed.
"We have... disappeared...?"
"Yes, you are no longer connected to the universe you were previously with."
"T-Then... where are we...? What are we... connected to?"
Ravana questioned. The shock on his face didn’t disappear for even a second. If anything, the absurdity of the words he was hearing rose further and further.
Just... what sort of people was he talking to...?
What in the hell was happening...?
"You are now in another universe, a place where the Supreme Worlds cannot reach you."
Shadow answered his question as she patted his shoulder with a reassuring nod, and Ravana—
"Even the Supreme Worlds... won’t be able to...?"
He obviously couldn’t believe what he was hearing.
Shadow, however, just nodded, and with a light smile on her face—
"Not just that, since you are no longer part of that universe, your world will no longer be affected every time the universe trembles."
"What...?"
Hearing those words, Ravana’s attitude changed instantly. Even if he somehow ignored the rest of the things he heard, this—he could not ignore.
"W-Will my world really not be affected by the trembling?"
He asked.
Honestly, he still did not understand how the things this woman mentioned were even possible, but when it came to his world and its safety, he... he wanted to believe her.
"Yes."
And Shadow, who knew his thoughts, nodded once again.
"You can now focus on recovering your world without having to worry about anything."
In an instant, Ravana felt such a strong sense of relief that the Progenitor barely stopped himself from collapsing.
"My... my world is saved..."
He muttered, his eyes that were once filled with fear and uncertainty now shined brightly with hope.
Soon, however, his hope collapsed as he thought of something else—
He spoke, his eyes turning towards the woman and—
"Why did you do all this? What... do you want in return?"
He asked.

Nothing in this universe was for free—the Greenmarch Progenitor knew that. If he was suddenly receiving so many favors at the same time, he was sure he needed to pay a price—a price that wouldn’t be low.
But then—
"Well, no reason in particular."
Shadow shrugged.
"Let’s say you were quite fortunate?"
"Fortunate...?"
Ravana blinked.
Was it truly... just him being fortunate...?
"Well, there is one thing I want in return."
Shadow spoke, and Ravana prepared himself to pay a big price.
His life, his freedom, anything—
"Your world’s will.
I need you to give me regular reports on its behavior from now on."
Shadow asked.
"Reports...?"
Ravana blinked again, and Shadow nodded again.
Nux didn’t save Greenmarch for a reason. Well, if one thought about it, it could be said he protected Greenmarch just so he could know whether he could actually protect it or not.
It was a test.
An experiment.
And after the experiment was complete, Shadow noticed another thing.
Because of their actions, Greenmarch had become... the first ’complete’ world of their universe.
Most worlds in their universe, no matter what level, were nothing more than a star—a source of energy for Nux.
While some of them did have living entities in them, those entities were incomplete.
Till now, only Umbrasol had true, complete life forms—no matter how simple—in it.
But now, Greenmarch was the same, and not just the same—Greenmarch was miles ahead. It didn’t just have simple life forms; it had complete, far more complicated life forms.
And Ravana...
He was the Progenitor of this world.
He had a direct connection with Greenmarch’s will—something even Shadow, the soul of the universe, did not have.
"Yes."
Shadow nodded.
"I want to know everything there is."
It was truly an offer where both parties didn’t lose anything—an offer no one would reject—
But—
"I... I don’t think I can help you."
Ravana shook his head.
"Huh?"
Shadow narrowed her eyes, and Ravana—
"I cannot properly sense Greenmarch’s will."
He revealed.
"What do you mean?"
Shadow questioned directly.
"The will is still there—that I can sense—but it is no longer answering my calls. It is as if... it is lying dormant."
This time, Shadow’s expression changed.
"A will of a world... lying dormant...?
But... that makes no sens—"
She muttered to herself. Soon, however, she froze.
Then suddenly, a playful voice was heard.
"It all makes sense now, doesn’t it, my love?"
Shadow, with her eyes wide open from the new possibility she had just figured out, turned towards Nux, who had appeared out of nowhere.
Then, she nodded.

"No wonder I couldn’t connect with the wills of the worlds inside our universe. If all the wills are dormant, then they wouldn’t possibly be able to answer me. That is no different than talking to an unconscious being."
Nux nodded at those words, agreeing with them.
Shadow, however, had another question in her head.
"But...
Why are all the world wills in this state?
They were fine when they were in the main universe, weren’t they?"
"That is because we completely changed their existence."
This time, the one who answered was Nux. After all, Shadow wasn’t the only one who was enlightened today.
"What do you mean?"
Shadow tried to ask—
BOOOOM
But before Nux could answer, his aura burst out and started getting stronger.
He...
He was ’leveling’ up again.

chapters.title: Chapter 2157: I can get stronger faster now.
paragraphs: "That is because we completely changed their existence."
Suddenly, Nux spoke up.
"What do you mean?"
Shadow tried to ask—
BOOOOM
But before Nux could answer, his aura burst out.
Then—
RUMBLE RUMBLE RUMBLE
THUNDER THUNDER THUNDER
The entire universe connected with Nux began to shake violently—Ravana, who was promised that his world would no longer be at risk of similar incidents, stared as his entire world shook.
"This..."
He glanced at Shadow, seeking protection, but Shadow had already moved—
With a wave of her hand, she forcefully suppressed Greenmarch’s tremors, saving the entire world from any damage.
And Ravana—he couldn’t believe it.
How...
This woman just did something that the artifact given by the Light Faction failed to do with a wave of her hand...
Just how was that possible...?
Shadow, however, completely ignored Ravana’s words. Her eyes were fixated on Nux. She quickly sensed her connection with him and began realizing what had just happened.
Nux...
He was getting stronger.
How?
Because he had once again ’understood’ his universe a little more than before.
A light smile appeared on Shadow’s face when she realized it. A few moments later, she too closed her eyes and—
BOOOM
Her aura exploded too.
Just like Nux, she was getting stronger as well.
A few minutes passed by in an instant. The sudden incident attracted a lot of attention, so much that all of Nux’s wives had already appeared.
Ravana, who saw all these women, felt... distant.
He was standing in their presence but didn’t dare to talk to any of them. To him, these beings felt... beyond him.
Beings he shouldn’t be standing together with.
The women didn’t spare him a glance either. Their eyes were only on Nux, waiting for him to open his eyes.
And soon, the wait ended.
"You got stronger."
Vyriana chuckled as Nux finally opened his eyes.
Nux nodded with a grin, feeling his strength. If before he was comparable to an early Transcendent, now he was a middle Transcendent.
The power didn’t sound—
It didn’t sound ’grand’, but for Nux, it was different.
He now understood his own powers much better than before. Not just that, he also had a stronger understanding of his universe.
Finally, Shadow called out as she opened her eyes.
"You still did not answer my question."
She mentioned.
The rest of the wives wanted to know as well.
"What do you mean we changed the Worlds’ Wills’ existence?"
Nux nodded at that question—
"The closest entities to a universe are its worlds."
He began. The women nodded at his words; this, they already knew.

"This is because the bond the universe and the worlds share is stronger than the bond the universe has with other entities—so much that it wouldn’t be wrong to call a world’s will a part of the universe’s will. It wouldn’t be wrong to say that a world’s will would not survive without the universe’s will."
Nux paused, staring at his wives as he let them absorb what he said.
"So unlike other living entities that don’t have much dependence on the universe’s will and can survive without it just fine,
when I devour a world, I devour a major component of its existence. This is the reason the wills of all the worlds I have devoured are dormant.
They are recovering from the damage I did to them.
They are... trying to complete themselves again."
"And... how can that be done...?"
Shadow asked carefully. As the soul of Nux’s universe—the closest thing to Nux’s universe’s will—she felt... responsible.
She felt that it was her duty to help the worlds’ wills recover from their states and be active again.
And Nux—
"You give them time."
He answered with a smile as he stared at Shadow, knowing exactly what she was thinking.
"They will recover eventually. Even if they have lost a major part of their existence, they have also gained a new one.
Our universe can support them just fine, just like it supports other living entities. They just need time to get used to this change."
"How much time?"
Felberta asked with a frown.
"It has been hundreds of years since we have devoured some of these worlds. How much more time do they need?"
She asked; she was particularly curious about this matter since it was related to creation—her own powers.
"That’s not the case."
Nux, however, shook his head.
"Yes, some of the worlds have been here for hundreds of years, but they weren’t in an environment where their wills could recover."
Felberta realized what Nux was trying to say.
"Incomplete universe..."
She muttered, and Nux nodded.

"Yes, our universe was incomplete. It wasn’t even in the state where it could grow itself or function independently. How could it be in a state for a world’s will to anchor itself with it and recover?"
"Does this mean the rest of the worlds will soon recover their wills as well?"
Evane asked curiously, and Nux nodded.
"How long would it take?"
The elf asked the same question.
"I don’t know, but it shouldn’t be that long."
"What would happen if the wills awaken?"
Vyriana asked another question. She wasn’t interested in learning about how the universe and the worlds’ wills worked; what she wanted to know was whether it would be beneficial to them in any way.
And the answer to that question—

"If it happens, the worlds would start giving birth to complicated life forms—life forms who could later start walking onto the cultivation bridge, and as these life forms grow stronger and achieve more breakthroughs..."
"You will get stronger."
Vyriana grinned.
"Exactly."
Nux nodded with the same grin.
"So this is the reason Umbrasol hasn’t given birth to a complicated life form yet, huh...
It needs a will."
Suddenly, Rune commented.
Nux turned towards the cat and nodded.
The cat then glanced at Ravana and—
"To think devouring a lowest-level world would reveal something so important and give us a way forward.
It was worth it."
She nodded, and for some reason, Ravana, despite not understanding a single thing that was mentioned here, bowed deeply, showing his gratitude and respect to the woman he didn’t even know.
But then—
"That wasn’t the only thing devouring Greenmarch like this gave us."
Nux commented with a smile.
"What...?"
The women tilted their heads, and Nux’s grin widened—
"Because I devoured all the life forms together with the world—
the amount of strength I gained is nearly twice compared to what I would usually gain after devouring a lowest-level world."
"Does this mean...?"
Astaria widened her eyes, and Nux, looking into her eyes, nodded again, his face distorting because of his grin.
"I can get stronger faster now."

chapters.title: Chapter 2158: [WHAT ARE YOU DOING!?]
paragraphs: "Did you find anything?"
Serion asked as another Light Born appeared in front of him, but this time, his usual calm was nowhere to be seen.
His breathing seemed a bit ragged, his hands held the Light Born’s shoulders in desperation, and his eyes searched for answers.
He needed an answer.
Something.
Anything would do.
Thirty minutes had passed. Eleven Light Borns had returned from their search, and none of them had brought any good news. At this point, Serion was at his wits’ end.
He needed to report back to the Supreme World quickly. If he didn’t find anything soon, this...
This might spell his end.
This was the reason he so desperately clung to the Light Born as if he were his last hope.
But...
The Light Born shook his head with a solemn look on his face, just like the others had.
"I searched a total of fifty worlds that had even the slightest bit of relationship with Greenmarch and its people, but I didn’t find any link to the Anomaly."
He explained.

Greenmarch was a lowest-level world. It had next to no connections to the rest of the worlds anyway because of how insignificant it was. But even then, these Light Borns forcefully found Greenmarch’s connection with other worlds. They even investigated the worlds the people of Greenmarch had visited once or twice.
Yes, even a link as weak as that was investigated, but...
The answer was still the same.
Nothing.
But of course, Serion couldn’t give up.
"Did yo—"
He tried speaking, but then—
RUMBLE RUMBLE RUMBLE
THUNDER THUNDER THUNDER
The familiar trembling began again.

Once again, the people of Gracevale stared above, their faces panicking. Of course, the protective artifacts given by the Supreme Factions were activated, avoiding any damages, but this was already the third time the universe had reacted. Not just the ordinary people of Gracevale—
Even the Light Borns themselves were alerted, scared even, especially Serion.
He was ordered to investigate the matter by the Light Infinity himself, but even after more than thirty minutes had passed, he had nothing.
What’s worse?
The universe was reacting again.
It meant that the enemy... was still active.
RUMBLE RUMBLE RUMBLE
THUNDER THUNDER THUNDERA grim look appeared on Serion’s face as he stared at the sky. The rest of the Light Borns had the same expressions as him.
And then suddenly—
Bzzz Bzzz Bzzz
Serion felt a buzz.
The artifact given to him by the Supreme World was trembling.
The Light Infinity...
He was contacting him. He wanted to know what Serion had found out, and Serion... he had no choice but to answer the call despite having nothing to say.
With shaking hands, he took out the Call Artifact from his dimensional storage, and the moment he picked up the call—
[WHAT ARE YOU DOING!?]
A shout was heard.
A shout that shook not just Serion but everyone around him. A voice so strong that anyone who was not a Light Born instantly collapsed the moment they heard it.
Within a single moment, the entirety of Gracevale passed out and turned silent like a wave.
"Lord Light..."
Serion tried to answer but—
[SERION! WHY HAVE I NOT RECEIVED ANY REPORTS YET!?]
The ’Lord Light’ questioned, his voice reflecting anger so strong that Serion couldn’t believe it. In his long life, this was probably the first time he had seen ’Lord Light’ act in such a manner.
Serion was scared, his body trembling without stop, but...
He still needed to answer.
And that is what he did—
"We... did not find anything."
He answered, his head remaining low as if Lord Light were standing right in front of him.
[What...?]
Hearing those words, ’Lord Light’ blinked. The immense anger in his voice was replaced by utter shock.
"The enemy left no trace. We searched everything, but there is no lead for us to work on."
Serion tried explaining the situation.
"Gracevale is clean, so I was thinking of starting from the beginning and investigating why the universe reacted just now."
He answered, trying to buy more time.
But—
[...Do you even know why the universe reacted again?]
Lord Light asked, his voice full of disbelief and anger.
"...I do not."
Serion answered honestly. He knew he couldn’t lie anyway.
[Didn’t you say you plan on investigating it?]
"I... haven’t acted yet."
Serion answered with hesitation. He very well knew that these words could get him killed, but he had no choice but to say them regardless.
"The enemy has ways we have never experienced before. Ordinary methods do not work on him. But please, Lord Light, give me a little more time.
I will make the enemy kneel right in front of you."

Serion spoke, clenching his fists as tightly as possible. Seeing a Light Born in such a state... it was probably a once-in-a-lifetime opportunity for most beings. Unfortunately, all of Gracevale’s people had already lost consciousness, so they couldn’t see it.
[Alrig—]
After a few moments of hesitation, Lord Light made a decision, but just as he was about to share it—
RUMBLE RUMBLE RUMBLE
THUNDER THUNDER THUNDER
It happened again.
The universe... trembled.
This time, much, much, much more than before.
The Light Borns who noticed it lost their minds, all of them staring at each other with absolute disbelief on their faces.
Just... just what was happening...
[Serion...]

Suddenly, Lord Light called out, his voice resembling that of a man who had lost everything. Something that the Light Borns would have noticed instantly and had their suspicions about, but right now, they too were too shaken to notice anything.
"Lord Light."
Serion bowed his head even deeper, waiting for further instructions.
[Do you know what just happened...?]
Lord Light questioned.
"I... I do not, Lord Light."
Serion shook his head. He didn’t even know why the universe trembled before—how was he supposed to know what happened now?
Even his connections had a limit, especially during a time like this, when every being in the universe was too awed, scared, or shocked to act normally.
[Dalestomb has disappeared.]
Lord Light informed, and the moment Serion heard the word Dalestomb, his expression changed.
"What...?"
He asked.
Dalestomb...?
How...?
Is the Anomaly... now targeting... High-Level Worlds...?𝐟𝗿𝐞𝚎𝚠𝐞𝚋𝕟𝐨𝚟𝐞𝕝.𝕔𝕠𝚖

chapters.title: Chapter 2159: Yes, Nux was now that strong.
paragraphs: [Dalestomb has disappeared.]
Lord Light informed, and the moment Serion heard the word Dalestomb, his expression changed.
"What...?"
He asked in complete disbelief. This, however, wasn’t the only news Lord Light was about to share.
[As for the trembling that happened before this...]
He began, his voice cracking a few times—something that, again, should not happen, but Serion and others were too overwhelmed to notice.
[It was because Glowreign had disappeared.]
Lord Light revealed, and the already shocked Serion widened his eyes even further, his mind so overwhelmed by everything he was told it was honestly a miracle that he hadn’t passed out.

Just like Dalestomb, Glowreign too was a High-Level World that belonged to the Light Faction. Even though these two weren’t particularly strong and only had one or two Eternal-Level beings leading them,
they, in the end, were still High-Level Worlds. For them to disappear like this, and that too, within minutes—
It was...
Something that had never happened before.
The Anomaly—the being who was only targeting Lowest, Low, and Middle-Level Worlds till now—was now targeting High-Level Worlds as well, and in no way was that good news.
[You said you wanted to investigate the disappearance of Glowreign.]
Lord Light muttered in a shaky voice.

[How are you going to investigate the world that doesn’t even exist anymore? Are you going to investigate its allies? How long will that take? What if the enemy targets and devours another world by then?
What...
What are we supposed to do now?]
Lord Light spoke, but this time, the shaken Serion finally noticed something he had been unknowingly ignoring all this time.
He frowned in confusion.
Did Lord Light just use the wordwe?
He as in him—the Lord Light—and him, Serion, together...?
That... that made Serion frown.
Lord Light was an Infinity-Level being—an Absolute.
A being who ruled over all of the Universe.
Someone like him would never lower himself and bring himself down to Serion’s level. He would definitely not mention his name as if the two of them were a ’team.’
Or could it be...
ThisLord Light... is not the Lord at all and someone else...?
The moment he thought about this possibility, Serion’s expression changed, but before he could think or do anything—
RUMBLE RUMBLE RUMBLE
THUNDER THUNDER THUNDER
Again.
The universe trembled again, this time even louder than before, as if enraged by being constantly targeted like this.
Serion glanced at the other Light Borns around him, each staring at him in disbelief. None of them could believe this was happening, but...
It was.
[I-It’s Heavenvein...]
Lord Light spoke with a stutter.
And this time, all Light Borns noticed it—his stuttering, his trembling voice.
The Lord Light was... scared.
And just that thought alone made them... widen their eyes, this time, not in shock but in horror.
If... even Lord Light was scared...
Then what was going to happen?
While the Light Borns back in Gracevale were losing their minds, on the other side, in an entirely different universe—
"You are being overly cautious today."
A woman hugged a man from behind and spoke in a low, melodious voice.
The man didn’t answer right away. He instead opened and closed his fists countless times, as if he couldn’t adjust to his own body.
"Did you get too strong again?"
Another woman asked.
The man turned towards her and nodded.
"Yeah, it happened too quickly..."
Hearing those words, the woman who was holding him from behind smiled. She gently moved her hands and held his.
"Don’t pretend as if you aren’t happy."
She chuckled.
"Who says I am not?"
The man grinned, overlapping his hands with hers.
"As for being cautious, it is better if we remain cautious till I am used to this. This is the first time someone challenged the authority of the Supreme Worlds so openly.
I am sure they must be losing their minds at this point. We do not know how quickly they might send reinforcements."
Nux explained.
"It is not like the reinforcements scare you. Even if they send a hundred Eternals, as long as they enter your domain, the battle is as good as over."
The woman who had hugged him from behind—Shadow—laughed again.
As someone who had the closest connection to Nux, she could tell just how much he had changed in just the last few minutes.
He had devoured three High-Level Worlds.
What’s even better?
Now that he could devour worlds completely—together with their living beings—the strength he gained from it was twice what he would normally gain.
So, in a way, Nux’s physical strength was currently six times greater compared to when he had just devoured Umbrasol.
Yes, he had turned into an absolute monster—to the point where even when Heavenvein’s Progenitor hit him with his strongest attack, he... didn’t even budge.
And that was all without him activating his domain and experiencing the Main Universe’s suppression.
Yes, Nux was nowthatstrong.
Even with the Main Universe suppressing him, most attacks of Eternal-Level beings would not even leave a scratch on him.
The only beings who could actively defeat him were...
"Eternals aren’t a problem. The more they come, the better, since they will only raise my army’s numbers even further.
The problem is... the Infinities."
Nux muttered, his face turning solemn.
"I still do not know whether I am strong enough to face them or not."

Once again, the problem was limited knowledge. He had devoured and read the memories of tens of Eternals, so he knew even the strongest Eternals wouldn’t be able to defeat him considering the level he had reached now.
However, because he had read so many memories, he knew that... Infinities were different.
No Eternal, no matter how strong, had ever managed to stand against an Infinity. The difference between them was simply too massive.
Honestly, even if Nux believed that he could now defeat an Infinity if he brought them to his universe, it wasn’t a risk he was willing to take. After all, one mistake here might ruin it all.
And Nux wasn’t foolish enough to make such a mistake.
So for now, the plan was simple—
"Let’s get as strong as possible, as cautiously as possible."
Nux muttered, and his wives around him smiled.
"Mm."
