chapters.title: Chapter 2160: Do not expect results which you yourself cannot produce.
paragraphs: RUMBLE RUMBLE RUMBLE
THUNDER THUNDER THUNDER
"What!? Again!?"
Serion widened his eyes in horror as he stared in a random direction. Around him was the endless void and multiple asteroids trembling violently, representing the universe’s anger.
Yes.
It happened again.
The universe was angry—another world had disappeared.
Serion too was no longer in Gracevale; he had already searched the entire world, read the memories of every single being present there, but the results were disappointing.
Nothing.
They found absolutely nothing about the enemy.
It was as if he appeared, attacked, took the Eternals, and disappeared.
What’s worse?
He was now committing far worse crimes than simply abducting Eternals.
Bzzz
While Serion, together with five other Light Borns following him, was moving toward one of the worlds that had disappeared in order to investigate—his call artifact trembled.
It was ’Lord Light’.
Serion picked up the call—
"Which one is it this time?"
He questioned. The other five Light Borns noticed how the respect in his tone had disappeared—an act that would instantly incinerate him if it was before, but now...
Instead of losing his temper and reacting violently, Lord Light informed,
[This time, i-it is not just one this time.
Three High-Level Worlds have disappeared.]
"What...?"
His words instantly made Serion and the others widen their eyes in absolute horror.

They had long gotten used to talking to Lord Light in such a tone. They weren’t fools—they all knew the being they were talking to was no Lord Light, but a mere representative, a representative who himself was in quite a difficult position now that things had gone south.
If anything, right now, the so-called ’Lord Light’ needed them the most. There was no way he would lose his temper over them talking to him in such a tone.

Honestly, if it were normal times, this would have been a moment all six of them would have enjoyed thoroughly—a being who ordered them around as if they were his dogs, now trembling and stuttering right in front of them.
Who would not find pleasure in such things?
But...
Right now, the words ’Lord Light’ said were too heavy, too impactful for their minds to even think about enjoying the moment.
If anything, they were all losing their minds.
After all, it was already—
[T-The enemy has already devoured fifteen High-Level Worlds!]
Lord Light shouted, his voice panicking, reflecting the horror he was currently going through.
Fifteen High-Level Worlds!
Of course, this wasn’t the first time something like this had happened. In fact, in the past, similar things had happened at an even greater scale—but the thing was...
That happened during the Faction Wars—wars where the Supreme Factions went all out against each other, to the point even the High-Level Worlds were affected and hundreds of them perished.
But...
Everything that happened back then took thousands of years.
But now...
Fifteen High-Level Worlds had disappeared in a mere few hours.
This was... absolutely ridiculous.
What’s worse?
They still had no lead.
The enemy was nowhere to be seen.
[Serion!]
Lord Light shouted.
[You need to get your act together! Collect yourself and find the enemy, or it will be the end of both of us!!]
At those words, however, a cold look appeared on Serion’s face.
"Don’t threaten me."
He spoke in a calm but heavy, harsh tone.
[W-What...?]
Lord Light’s voice shook, as if he couldn’t believe what just happened.
"I said do not threaten me."
Serion repeated.
"The enemy is too mysterious, his ways are beyond what we can currently comprehend. He does not leave any traces when he moves; there is no pattern in his movements for us to track him.
It is impossible to find and capture him.
We do not have the means.
Yet my men are still giving their all. They have flipped the entire universe apart in order to search for the enemy, and they will find him eventually—
But you need to give me and them some time.
Do not expect results which you yourself cannot produce."
Saying those words, Serion cut off the communication and stored the Call Artifact back in his dimensional storage.
Then, without wasting his time, he stared in the direction he was moving and—
"Move."
He ordered.
The other Light Borns around him nodded and followed him without asking further questions. Their goal was already clear in their heads.
On the other side, inside a chamber that glowed with soft, endless light, sat a being of light.

He had no face, no eyes, no solid form. His body was shaped like a man, yet he seemed made of pure light. His glow shifted between gold and white, even the sacred marble beneath him hummed, unable to bear his presence in silence.
This was... ’Lord Light’, currently sitting in the Hall of Radiance—the most sacred place within the Light Temple—a room where even sound dared not disturb the air.

Every inch of it shimmered with purity. The walls, made of living crystal, pulsed faintly with gold and white hues. Golden inscriptions flowed across the surfaces in quiet motion, retelling stories of the universe’s creation and the first dawn that gave birth to the Supreme World of Light.

At the far end of the hall stood the only statue ever permitted within the temple—a statue carved entirely from pure sunlight crystal. She stood with her hands gently raised toward the heavens, her expression calm and kind, her eyes closed in eternal peace. The light around her shimmered softly, as if the temple itself still breathed through her memory.

At the center stood a circular platform of white marble, smooth as still water. Around it, hundreds of tall pillars rose like frozen sunbeams. Above, a halo of light drifted endlessly, rotating so slowly it seemed to stop time itself.
Lord Light sat at the very center. In front of him floated a large orb.

The orb pulsed softly with golden light—it was the Orb of Communion, a relic used by the Supreme World of Light to speak across endless distances. Its surface was smooth like glass, and inside it swirled tens of thousands of living stars—each one a link to another Light Born.
And from the orb came a voice—
[Do not expect results which you yourself cannot produce.]
It was Serion’s.
And when Lord Light realized what had happened and noticed how the star representing Serion dulled a little, showing that he had ended the connection—
"W-What...?"
He couldn’t believe what happened.
Did... did that child just cut off the communication with him?

sentences.text: RUMBLE RUMBLE RUMBLE
THUNDER THUNDER THUNDER
"What!?
Again!?"
Serion widened his eyes in horror as he stared in a random direction.
Around him was the endless void and multiple asteroids trembling violently, representing the universe’s anger.
Yes.
It happened again.
The universe was angry—another world had disappeared.
Serion too was no longer in Gracevale; he had already searched the entire world, read the memories of every single being present there, but the results were disappointing.
Nothing.
They found absolutely nothing about the enemy.
It was as if he appeared, attacked, took the Eternals, and disappeared.
What’s worse?
He was now committing far worse crimes than simply abducting Eternals.
Bzzz
While Serion, together with five other Light Borns following him, was moving toward one of the worlds that had disappeared in order to investigate—his call artifact trembled.
It was ’Lord Light’.
Serion picked up the call—
"Which one is it this time?"
He questioned.
The other five Light Borns noticed how the respect in his tone had disappeared—an act that would instantly incinerate him if it was before, but now...
Instead of losing his temper and reacting violently, Lord Light informed,
[This time, i-it is not just one this time.
Three High-Level Worlds have disappeared.]
"What...?"
His words instantly made Serion and the others widen their eyes in absolute horror.
They had long gotten used to talking to Lord Light in such a tone.

They weren’t fools—they all knew the being they were talking to was no Lord Light, but a mere representative, a representative who himself was in quite a difficult position now that things had gone south.
If anything, right now, the so-called ’Lord Light’ needed them the most.
There was no way he would lose his temper over them talking to him in such a tone.

Honestly, if it were normal times, this would have been a moment all six of them would have enjoyed thoroughly—a being who ordered them around as if they were his dogs, now trembling and stuttering right in front of them.
Who would not find pleasure in such things?
But...
Right now, the words ’Lord Light’ said were too heavy, too impactful for their minds to even think about enjoying the moment.
If anything, they were all losing their minds.
After all, it was already—
[T-The enemy has already devoured fifteen High-Level Worlds!]
Lord Light shouted, his voice panicking, reflecting the horror he was currently going through.
Fifteen High-Level Worlds!
Of course, this wasn’t the first time something like this had happened.
In fact, in the past, similar things had happened at an even greater scale—but the thing was...
That happened during the Faction Wars—wars where the Supreme Factions went all out against each other, to the point even the High-Level Worlds were affected and hundreds of them perished.
But...
Everything that happened back then took thousands of years.
But now...
Fifteen High-Level Worlds had disappeared in a mere few hours.
This was... absolutely ridiculous.
What’s worse?
They still had no lead.
The enemy was nowhere to be seen.
[Serion!]
Lord Light shouted.
[You need to get your act together!
Collect yourself and find the enemy, or it will be the end of both of us!!]
At those words, however, a cold look appeared on Serion’s face.
"Don’t threaten me."
He spoke in a calm but heavy, harsh tone.
[W-What...?]
Lord Light’s voice shook, as if he couldn’t believe what just happened.
"I said do not threaten me."
Serion repeated.
"The enemy is too mysterious, his ways are beyond what we can currently comprehend.
He does not leave any traces when he moves; there is no pattern in his movements for us to track him.
It is impossible to find and capture him.
We do not have the means.
Yet my men are still giving their all.
They have flipped the entire universe apart in order to search for the enemy, and they will find him eventually—
But you need to give me and them some time.
Do not expect results which you yourself cannot produce."
Saying those words, Serion cut off the communication and stored the Call Artifact back in his dimensional storage.
Then, without wasting his time, he stared in the direction he was moving and—
"Move."
He ordered.
The other Light Borns around him nodded and followed him without asking further questions.
Their goal was already clear in their heads.
On the other side, inside a chamber that glowed with soft, endless light, sat a being of light.
He had no face, no eyes, no solid form.
His body was shaped like a man, yet he seemed made of pure light.
His glow shifted between gold and white, even the sacred marble beneath him hummed, unable to bear his presence in silence.
This was... ’Lord Light’, currently sitting in the Hall of Radiance—the most sacred place within the Light Temple—a room where even sound dared not disturb the air.
Every inch of it shimmered with purity.
The walls, made of living crystal, pulsed faintly with gold and white hues.
Golden inscriptions flowed across the surfaces in quiet motion, retelling stories of the universe’s creation and the first dawn that gave birth to the Supreme World of Light.
At the far end of the hall stood the only statue ever permitted within the temple—a statue carved entirely from pure sunlight crystal.
She stood with her hands gently raised toward the heavens, her expression calm and kind, her eyes closed in eternal peace.
The light around her shimmered softly, as if the temple itself still breathed through her memory.
At the center stood a circular platform of white marble, smooth as still water.
Around it, hundreds of tall pillars rose like frozen sunbeams.
Above, a halo of light drifted endlessly, rotating so slowly it seemed to stop time itself.
Lord Light sat at the very center.
In front of him floated a large orb.
The orb pulsed softly with golden light—it was the Orb of Communion, a relic used by the Supreme World of Light to speak across endless distances.
Its surface was smooth like glass, and inside it swirled tens of thousands of living stars—each one a link to another Light Born.
And from the orb came a voice—
[Do not expect results which you yourself cannot produce.]
It was Serion’s.
And when Lord Light realized what had happened and noticed how the star representing Serion dulled a little, showing that he had ended the connection—
"W-What...?"
He couldn’t believe what happened.
Did... did that child just cut off the communication with him?

chapters.title: Chapter 2161: Thank you for the meal.
paragraphs: [Do not expect results which you yourself cannot produce.]
Serion’s voice was heard before he cut the call, and in an instant—Lord Light froze.
"W-What...?"
He let out a word, unable to believe what had just happened.
Did... did that child just cut off communication with him?

He wondered in his head, his mind unable to comprehend this. The impossibility of such an action was simply too absolute in his mind for him to even consider otherwise. Soon, however, realization kicked in.
He... that child did cut contact on his own.
The memories of the conversation they had held in the past few hours—the one he hadn’t properly noticed since he had countless other things to worry about—finally resurfaced in his mind.
His trembling, panicking voice, his commands that sounded less like commands and more like him begging for help...
Lord Light recalled it all.
The fear had consumed him so much that he actually allowed a child to look down on him...
He couldn’t believe it.
Slowly, he turned towards the statue at the far end of the Hall and—
"Lady Seraphielle..."
He muttered in a soft voice, as if all his panic and fear instantly disappeared the instant he took that name.
"What have I done...?"
He muttered to himself.
"I took the title of Lord Light by your command, and today... because of my short-sightedness and fear... I... tarnished it.
I let a Light Born treat me with disrespect."
He spoke, his words echoing throughout the room. His remorse couldn’t be clearer.
"Please,
Please forgive your child."
He begged as he bowed his head, and at the same time, he made up his mind.
Serion—he needed to perish.
He had let the Light Born walk over him in such a manner; it was time to show him his place. And yes, ’Lord Light’ was very much capable of doing so.

Yes, Serion was an Eternal—one of the strongest beings in the entirety of the universe—but in front of ’Lord Light’, he was merely a flickering star whose life and death could be decided with just a wave of his hand.
That was who ’Lord Light’ was.
The Ultimate Being—the being who served as the bridge between the Light Infinity and the Light Borns.
The being who commanded the Supreme World of Light on behalf of the Light Infinity, Lady Seraphielle.
A being who was below one and above all.
That was who Lord Light was.
He wasn’t particularly strong; in fact, he was not strong at all. He only had one ability—even a mere Transcendent would be physically stronger than him—but...
Lord Light was a beingmadeby the Light Infinity herself. As long as he was in the Supreme World of Light, under Light Infinity’s domain—he couldn’t be killed.
As for his ability—
It was the ability to control and decide the fate of the ’Stars’ inside the Orb of Communication.
Yes, Lord Light had power over the Orb of Communication—the power to communicate with any Star, or in other words, any Light Born, whenever he desired.
However, ’communication’ wasn’t the only thing his ability was limited to.

Just as mentioned before, he could control and decide the fate of these Stars. If he wanted to remove their memories, he could. If he wanted to add false memories to their heads, he could. Even if he wanted to take control over a said star’s body, he could—without effort.
This was the power Lord Light held.
Absolute power—where if he wanted one of the stars to disappear, it would.
He was even capable of killing all Light Borns with just a thought. So even if he himself wasn’t strong, for the Light Borns...
He was absolute.
And he was going to show that by making an example out of Serion.

He would give him an agonizing death, and he would make sure that every single Light Born—be it one who was born only a few hundred thousand years ago or the ones who had been roaming since the start of time itself—saw it all.𝙛𝒓𝒆𝙚𝒘𝒆𝓫𝙣𝓸𝙫𝓮𝒍.𝒄𝒐𝓶
With that thought strengthening in his mind, Lord Light prepared himself and singled out the star that represented Serion.
But just then—
The Orb of Communication started glowing. Lord Light noticed one of the stars shining brightly, meaning one of the Light Borns was trying to contact him, and when he accepted the call—
[I see him! The Anomaly! He is right in front of me!]
A voice was heard, and in an instant, Lord Light’s body language changed.
Serion’s matter could be dealt with later—but this was something he couldn’t delay.
Without waiting even a single moment, he ’grabbed’ the star he was talking to and decided to take over his body.
Very quickly, his surroundings changed. Now, he was no longer in the temple, but in a void, in front of another High-Level World named Craya—and in front of him stood...
Him.
The Anomaly.
Lord Light noticed that his body was using an artifact to keep itself hidden, so the Anomaly hadn’t noticed him yet—and he wanted to keep it that way.
He had no plans of letting the enemy escape, so he wouldn’t make a move unless he was completely ready.
Within a few milliseconds, Lord Light acted. He once again returned to the temple and moved around a hundred stars, placing them close to the star he had just possessed.
Yes, he had forcefully teleported one hundred and three Light Borns to where the Anomaly was, despite the space being sealed in that area.
Then, without wasting any time, he once again possessed the Light Born’s body, prepared for the final battle—but—
The only thing he heard was—
"Thank you for the meal."
And then—
His vision turned dark.
"Aaaggh!!"
When Lord Light opened his eyes again, he realized he had once again returned to the temple.
Yes, he had been sent back forcefully.
He thought of going back again, but then suddenly—
RUMBLE RUMBLE RUMBLE
THUNDER THUNDER THUNDER
The universe trembled again, and in an instant, Lord Light froze.
He... he had a bad feeling about this...

chapters.title: Chapter 2162: We are coming for you.
paragraphs: "I... I was sent back...?"
Lord Light muttered in utter disbelief as he opened his eyes and realized that he was back in the Temple.
Just... how was this possible...?
He couldn’t believe it.
Did... the Anomaly know he was there?
But even if he knew, these stars weren’t connected to the Light Borns in the normal manner; these stars were... a part of their soul.
They were formed the moment they were born—no power in the universe should be able to break the connection between the Stars and the Light Borns.
And Lord Light, who had absolute control over these Stars... it should be impossible for his connection to a Light Born to break, no matter what the enemy did.
Unless...
’No, that isn’t possible.
The battle hadn’t even started yet.’
Lord Light shook his head, and the moment all these thoughts appeared in his head, they disappeared as well. He knew this wasn’t the time to think of such matters.
He needed to return.
He needed more information on the enemy.
With that thought in his mind, he leaned forward, wanting to return, but then suddenly—
RUMBLE RUMBLE RUMBLE
THUNDER THUNDER THUNDER
The universe trembled again.
—and Lord Light froze.
"What...?"
He let out a word; the possibility he considered before reappeared in his mind, and a chill ran through his body.
He leaned forward with a tense body, looking into the orb, and the moment he did—
He took a deep breath, and his tense body grew even tenser.
It... it actually happened...
A total of one hundred and four stars had disappeared from the Orb.
Yes, these were the same Light Borns he had teleported to face the enemy—they... they were all dead—or in this case, devoured.
’But how...?’
Lord Light couldn’t believe it.
More than a hundred Light Borns... just like that?
None of these Light Borns were weak; they were all Eternals who were at least a few million years old, experienced and stronger than most beings in the world.
To take down a hundred such enemies... that too... in less than a second...
The enemy...
It was clear.𝗳𝚛𝚎𝚎𝘄𝕖𝕓𝕟𝕠𝚟𝚎𝕝.𝗰𝕠𝐦
Lord Light gulped.
The enemy was an Infinity...
It wasn’t a threat he could deal with on his own.
Slowly, he turned towards the statue at the far end of the Hall—
"Lady Se—"
He tried to call out, but then—
[L-Lord Light.]
A voice was heard.
One of the Stars in the Orb began shining brightly, interrupting him midway. Lord Light froze, slowly turning around, waiting for the Light Born to continue.
[Y-You need to see this for yourself.]
The Light Born answered. From his voice, it seemed like he didn’t even wish to explain what was happening.
Lord Light frowned at that. He stared at the ’Star’ he was talking to carefully and realized that it was a Light Born who had been sent to investigate one of the worlds that had been devoured.
With the frown still on his face, Lord Light once again extended his hand, accessing the shining star and possessing the Light Born’s body.
Once again, his surroundings changed—and there—he saw it.
A ridiculously huge projection of a handsome being.
A tall man cloaked in black and silver robes, a ridiculously handsome face, and golden eyes that Lord Light instantly recognized.
He...
He was the same man who had challenged the Supreme Worlds before, the voice that represented those bold but foolish people...
The Chain Breakers.
[A good day to you all.]
He began, his greeting similar to before.
[I hope you have not forgotten me.]
He smiled charmingly, staring right into Lord Light’s eyes, as if he was aware that he could see him.
[A few hours ago, I came before all of you, taking responsibility for the destruction of fifty-six Mercenary Worlds—that was when I made you aware of our little group and our intention.

And as one would expect, many of you mocked us, many didn’t believe us, many called us crazy, many thought we were overstepping our boundaries, many just waited for us to be crushed like the bugs we were—]
The man’s golden eyes then turned cold, reflecting a merciless light—
[Many looked down on us.]
He spoke, and Lord Light, who was hearing those words, stared at the scene wide-eyed, his body trembling ever so slightly.
[Our message was spread, discussed amongst people like we wanted it to be, but... it wasn’t done to spread awareness—it was done to mock us.

It made us realize how deeply trillions upon trillions of years of slavery have affected the minds of common people. Even people who aren’t directly involved with the Supreme Worlds laughed at us and actively looked forward to the Supreme Worlds crushing us—
And this led us to make our second move faster than we originally planned.]
The man took a deep breath, as if letting the listeners prepare for what was about to come.
[I said it before,
We will destroy every world that bows to you.
We will erase every being that serves you.
We will drag your name through blood and ash.
We will show your so-called ’followers’ what happens when they put faith in false gods.
And that is exactly what we did—
Fifteen.
Fifteen Worlds, and not just any worlds—fifteen High-Level Worlds, worlds that the oh-so-great Supreme Faction cherishes the most—
We destroyed them.]
He spoke as he clenched his fists, a wild, unfiltered grin appearing on his face. The man then finally looked back into Lord Light’s eyes again and—
[And you know the most exciting part?
When we were destroying the worlds the Supreme Factions cherished so much, the Supreme Worlds—the so-called ’protectors of the universe’—were utterly helpless.
They did nothing.
Just like I said before.
Because the truth still hasn’t changed.
You, the oh-so-mighty ’Supreme Worlds’—
Cannot protect what’s yours.]
Nux’s grin then widened even further, his face distorting in a terrifying manner—
[The oh-so-mighty ’Supreme’ Worlds—it has begun.
From here on out,
Your rule will rot.
Your influence will burn.
And your name...
It will no longer command fear, but suspicion and doubt.
Because from this day forth,
We, the Chain Breakers, declare an all-out war.
Every single world in the universe that is even remotely connected to the Supreme Worlds—be prepared,
We are coming for you.
And keep it in your mind—
Your protectors won’t protect you.
Just like they couldn’t protect the worlds I destroyed today.]

When we were destroying the worlds the Supreme Factions cherished so much, the Supreme Worlds—the so-called ’protectors of the universe’—were utterly helpless.
They did nothing.
Just like I said before.
Because the truth still hasn’t changed.
You, the oh-so-mighty ’Supreme Worlds’—
Cannot protect what’s yours.]
Nux’s grin then widened even further, his face distorting in a terrifying manner—
[The oh-so-mighty ’Supreme’ Worlds—it has begun.
From here on out,
Your rule will rot.
Your influence will burn.
And your name...
It will no longer command fear, but suspicion and doubt.
Because from this day forth,
We, the Chain Breakers, declare an all-out war.
Every single world in the universe that is even remotely connected to the Supreme Worlds—be prepared,
We are coming for you.
And keep it in your mind—
Your protectors won’t protect you.
Just like they couldn’t protect the worlds I destroyed today.]

chapters.title: Chapter 2163: So she’s awake, huh…
paragraphs: [Every single World in the Universe that is even remotely connected to the Supreme Worlds—be prepared,
We are coming for you,
And keep it in your mind—
Your protectors won’t protect you.
Just like they couldn’t protect the Worlds I destroyed today.]
Saying those words, the projection began to flicker; the recording had ended.
Lord Light, who was currently possessing the Light Born’s body, stood absolutely frozen, overwhelmed by what he had just seen.
He opened his mouth, but no words came out—his mind became a mess.
Fifteen Worlds, more than a hundred Light Borns...
He had lost too much in too little time. All this, combined with an open declaration of war like this...
If before, the people took those words lightly—joking and laughing on the matter—now, it was a direct slap on the face of the Supreme Worlds.
High-Level Worlds were destroyed; this was no longer a laughing matter.
The enemy... was strong.𝓯𝙧𝓮𝓮𝒘𝓮𝙗𝙣𝒐𝒗𝒆𝓵.𝓬𝓸𝒎
Flicker Flicker Flicker
[A good day to you all.]

While Lord Light was thinking all this, the flickering projection started the same speech again. He narrowed his eyes and saw a small artifact. With a wave of his hand, the artifact appeared in his hand, and with a single look, he understood that this thing was made to run the same recording again and again for hundreds of years.
Crack

Without wasting any time, Lord Light crushed the artifact. It was a particularly simple one to make, one almost any creator could make, so he knew he would get no information regarding the enemy through this.
In the end, Lord Light sighed again and closed his eyes, returning to the temple with a solemn look on his face.
This wasn’t the time to be shocked or lose his calm—it was the time to act.
However, the moment he returned—
[Lord Light—you need to see this!]
[Lord Light!]
[Something happened!]
[They challenged us to War!]
Almost every Light Born he had sent out began reporting the matter through the orb, talking over each other.

Only the Eternal Level Light Borns who were more than a million years old were relatively silent—not because they were calmer or more experienced in matters related to war, but because they knewsomethingwas about to happen.
Something big.
And they were right—
It began.
Flicker Flicker Flicker
The light within the Hall of Radiance flickered for the first time in a long, long time.
A soft tremor passed through the marble floor, so faint at first that even the golden inscriptions along the crystal walls did not notice. But then—
Crack
A hairline fracture ran through the base of the only statue in the temple—the statue of the woman carved from sunlight crystal.
Lord Light, seated before the Orb of Communion, froze.
His luminous form turned sharply toward the sound, his golden radiance dimming in disbelief.
Rumble Rumble Rumble
The statue trembled again. This time, the light from its surface flared brighter—too bright, even for the Hall of Radiance.
The Light Inscriptions carved into the walls began to move, glowing faster and faster, circling the statue as though bowing before their true master.
Lord Light stood from his throne of gold, his usually calm aura wavering with awe and fear.
"...I-It’s happening,"
He whispered, his voice trembling.
The air in the Temple thickened; the sacred marble beneath his feet began to glow, cracks of light spreading outward like veins of living gold.
The halo above the hall descended, surrounding the statue in endless radiance.
And then—
The statue’s still face blinked.
Stone turned to flesh, light turned to life, and what once was cold crystal became the most breathtaking being the Universe had ever known.
Seraphielle Light—the Infinity of Light—was awake.
Flap
Her wings unfolded with a whisper—a sound that seemed to resemble the hymn of creation itself.
Each feather gleamed like molten gold, reflecting the very essence of Light’s existence.
Her skin glowed faintly, warm and flawless, like dawn caught in eternal stillness.
Her long and luminous hair cascaded around her in waves of pure light, every strand moving as if it were alive.
And finally—
The woman opened her eyes—eyes that carried the light of millions of golden stars.
Her beauty transcended any race, any form—as if her very existence represented the concept of beauty itself.
She was perfection given shape—the reason the wordbeautyeven existed.
Her golden gown flowed like liquid light, adorned with markings of language most beings wouldn’t recognize.
Every movement she made, even the faintest tilt of her head, sent ripples of Light Energy through the room.
As she hovered above the platform, the halo that once hung above the temple now rested behind her—spinning, brilliant, alive.
"Lady Seraphielle..."
Lord Light fell to one knee instantly, his head bowed in absolute reverence, his light dimming before her radiant presence.
"You have returned."
He whispered, his voice shaking between awe and devotion.
Seraphielle looked down at him. Her gaze remained soft, as if everything that had happened did not have even the slightest impact on her.
The golden light around her shimmered like dawn breaking after endless night.
"Rise."
She spoke.
Her voice was serene—soft, melodic, yet layered with a power that could rewrite existence.
Lord Light stood up at her words, following her command. The divine being nodded ever so slightly until finally, she started looking around.
Millions, if not billions, of years had passed since she was last awakened—when was the last time again?
When she faced Zylarith?
Maybe.
But all that did not matter right now.
First, she needed to understand why she was awake in the first place.
With that thought in her mind, she raised her hand and flicked her fingers. With a gesture as simple as that—

In a room with a ridiculously large table and four incomprehensible entities hovering on each side of the table, one of the entities—the golden-colored one—began to tremble before it flickered out of existence, disappearing from the cosmic room.
And the other three entities that were left—
They all turned towards each other and—
"So she’s awake, huh..."
"Does this mean we will be waking up soon as well?"
"Things are... getting complicated..."

chapters.title: Chapter 2164: The Shadows have forgotten their place.
paragraphs: Millions, if not billions, of years had passed since she was last woken up—when was the last time again?
When she faced Zylarith?
Maybe.
But that did not matter right now.
First, she needed to understand why she was awake in the first place.
With that thought in her mind, she raised her hand in a graceful, effortless manner, and with a soft flick of her fingers—
Whoosh

The golden light around her shifted, folding inward, and Seraphielle slowly closed her eyes, as if prepared to accept what was coming. Even an action as simple as this carried such grace that Lord Light, who was witnessing everything with his own eyes, felt... at peace.
It was so different from the constant chaotic thoughts he had in his head that he felt like... he was bewitched.
He couldn’t move his eyes away from Lady Seraphielle, and this feeling was so strong that it felt like even if the very temple itself fell, that wouldn’t change.
Lady Seraphielle’s Aura was... simply unfathomable.
For a heartbeat, even the temple itself fell silent. There was no sound, no hum, no movement—only absolute stillness, as if anticipating what was about to come.
And finally—
It happened.
Fwooom

A wave of golden flickering energy burst from her body, spreading through the Hall of Radiance like a tide of pure divinity. Her form seemed to dissolve into that very brilliance, her body and light merging together until she became one with the golden radiance itself.
The temple brightened beyond reason—walls, ceiling, even the sacred inscriptions vanished under the flood of light.
Lord Light shielded his eyes out of instinct, yet even his radiant form felt... small, fragile, and unworthy beneath her true presence.
The marble beneath Seraphielle melted into liquid gold. The halo behind her spun faster, expanding until it engulfed the entire temple.
As the light surged outward, every being within the Light Temple felt it—a holy pressure... pure, graceful, peaceful, yet... crushing.
And in an instant, every being in the Supreme World of Light realized it—
This...
This was the return of Light.
Whoosh

The golden radiance expanded even further, touching every corner of the Supreme World of Light, pouring into the skies, escaping through the clouds—before it spread through the very fabric of the Universe.
The Light Borns outside gasped, falling to their knees.
The dark Universe Void was split with golden lines; the stars brightened, constellations realigned. Every living being felt the pure power of light spreading around them—no matter how far they were.
Yes, every being in the Universe could feel her.
Something had happened.
Something... had awakened.
And considering how this had happened right after they were done watching the Chain Breakers’ announcement... they all realized what was happening.
The Supreme Worlds were making a move.
And the beings throughout the rest of the Universe—those who could understand what was happening—held their breaths.
This was... thebeginning.
Whoosh Whoosh Whoosh
Within the temple, the golden energy around Seraphielle began to condense.
Slowly, gracefully, her perfect, divine form that seemed untouched by even time itself returned.
But this time, her eyes—her eyes blazed brighter than before. The light they carried before now seemed... insignificant.
Now, her eyes reflected understanding.

Golden ripples spread across her mind like pages of history unfolding—the fragments of wars, trillions and trillions of prayers, her final battle against Zylarith, and the Anomaly that challenged their Authority—all returned at once.
She whispered softly, her voice echoing through both the temple and beyond.
"Someone dared to challenge us after all these years..."
She smiled faintly, though there was no warmth in her expression—it was only... amusement.
"...This is certainly amusing."

Lord Light trembled where he stood. His radiance faltered, almost fading away as he stood in Seraphielle’s presence. Even though she had not released a drop of killing intent, the weight of her words seemed to press against his soul itself.
Seraphielle, however, did not know he was going through all that—or maybe she knew; she just... did not care.
She just... flicked her hand again.
That was all it was.
Just a flick.
Nothing more.
But...
WHOOOOM
The entire Universe responded.
Entire galaxies slowed for a heartbeat, stars flickered, and even worlds untouched by Light felt their oceans shimmer with gold.
Across countless stars, trillions and trillions of light-years ahead, every Light Born—who was sent to investigate different regions—suddenly froze.
Their eyes widened as a flood of memories poured into them—ancient, buried memories that had been sealed away for eons.
Visions of Seraphielle’s last battle, the final confrontation with Zylarith, the day she had fallen into slumber.
Her voice, her image, her power—they remembered everything.
Her face, which was once an indistinct, incomprehensible blur in their minds, now appeared crystal clear.
Her name—something they did not even know a second ago—now burned like fire upon their tongues.
Even the younger Light Borns, the ones who hadn’t experienced the previous Grand War of the Five Supreme Worlds, learned of Seraphielle’s existence.
It was as if... a part of the Light Borns that was sealed deep within had now returned.
The Light Borns... were nowcomplete.
"Lady Seraphielle..."
Every Light Born trembled.
Their wings spread wide, their halos flared, their hearts filled with awe and reverence.
She was awake.
The Light Infinity—Seraphielle Light—had returned.
And then—
"My children."
Her voice echoed through the cosmos.
She didn’t need any artifact or a link to communicate—her voice traveled through Light itself, able to reach every single world, every single city, every single being throughout the Universe.
Yes, the Light Infinity was now addressing the entire Universe.
"Your cries have reached me."𝒇𝒓𝒆𝒆𝙬𝒆𝒃𝓷𝒐𝓿𝙚𝙡.𝒄𝓸𝒎
She spoke softly, her tone deepened—majestic and calm, like the final light of dawn addressing the night.
"For too long, I let it go.
What happened, I let it happen, thinking the intelligence and free will the Universe bestowed upon them would let them understand and find the right path on their own.
I believed peace would hold this fragile Universe together.
Yet...
My thoughts were proven wrong.
The guilty did not repent.
The cruel did not reflect.
And the Shadows—
The Shadows have forgotten their place."

chapters.title: Chapter 2165: The Light will shine again
paragraphs: "The guilty did not repent.
The cruel did not reflect.
And the Shadows—
The Shadows have forgotten their place."
Those words echoed throughout the Universe, heard by every single being, be it in the Faction of Light, Darkness, Eternity, or Balance.

Even those who weren’t directly or even indirectly linked with any of these Factions—even those who were learning of the very existence of the Supreme World of Light for the first time—heard her voice.

The golden radiance that carried her words still rippled through the cosmos. Worlds glowed like stars, suns dimmed before her light, and even the void itself seemed to shimmer, unable to reject her presence.
In every corner of existence—be it worlds of flame, oceans of mist, or the frozen cities drifting through eternity—they all felt her presence.
It... it felt like the Universe itself was allowing it to happen.
"My children,"
Seraphielle spoke again.
"The storm you feel... is not the end.
It is but a ripple—a shadow’s last cry before it fades."
Her words carried heavy, commanding warmth. A contradiction in itself, it was like... the warm, comfortable embrace of sunlight that was too bright to endure.
"Their challenge, their blasphemy... was not made against you.
It was made against us—against the Light that has guided all life since the first spark."
Seraphielle’s gaze drifted beyond the temple, as if she could see the countless beings who were awed by her presence.
"They believe themselves free because theybroke the chainsthey imagined.
But tell me—
What freedom is born from defiance of order?
What strength lies in hatred of the hand that protects?"
Her vast and radiant wings unfurled.
"They call themselves Chain Breakers.
And yet, in breaking what binds, they have only shattered what shields.
They have brought not liberty—but chaos.
They have not defied darkness—they have become it."
Her golden aura pulsed outward again, strengthening around the entire Universe as every being felt even closer to her.
Almost as if... it was inescapable.
"I will not allow it."
She declared, her voice carried absolute authority, as if her words alone were more than enough to stop everything that had happened.
Even the Universe’s anger seemed to have calmed down ever since she released her aura. This was also the reason the Universe was actively supporting her to spread her message.
And Seraphielle had no intention of letting this chance go.
"The Light does not abandon its creation.
It has not done so in the past—
It will not do so now."
Across millions of worlds, people fell silent, listening to her words intensely.
After everything that had happened, after how the Universe’s constant angry fits left most of them in shambles, desperate for help, these words became... hope.
This was... such a strong display of power and authority that even the proudest Eternals lowered their heads.
This was not the speech of a ruler—it was... the declaration of existence itself.
Seraphielle raised her hand slightly, and the radiance grew warmer.
"For eons, I trusted Balance.
I trusted the others to keep their promise—to guard this Universe as we once swore together."
Her words flowed gently. She didn’t accuse anyone, she didn’t blame anyone—or at least, that was the illusion her tone and gentleness created.
"Balance, however, is now broken."
But deep down—her words were sharper than any blade.
"It claims neutrality and calls it peace.
But peace without action is decay.
It watched as the scales tilted and called it equilibrium.
It watched as the innocent bled and called it destiny."
She paused for a slight moment, letting her words sink in before—
"The Universe does not need watchers.
It needs guardians."
She declared, her voice filled with reassurance.
But the Infinity of Light wasn’t yet done—
"Then comes Eternity.
It dwells in the archives of forever, studying what has been and what will be. Its wisdom is indeed unmatched, yet...
In search for meaning,
It forgot... compassion."
She spoke, her tone carried no anger, only disappointment so profound that even the Eternity Borns trembled and lowered their heads in guilt.
"The Universe doesn’t need scholars to know it all. It does not need scholars who scavenge through historic records and predict billions of unpredictable future possibilities—
It needs beings who learn from history and prevent the same mistakes from happening again. It needs beings who stand when the very existence of the Universe is under threat."
The Infinity of Light muttered. Her words earned trillions and trillions of nods.
Her ideas of compassion and mercy began to spread, and now, when the time was most optimal—
"And Darkness..."
She breathed, her tone shifting for the first time. She was still calm, but this time, it was filled with judgment.
"It disappointed me the least."
She began—her words contrary to what the Darkness Borns were expecting to hear. But then—
"What was born from silence and death, what thrives in destruction, death, and wars, what spreads fear and names it power—what else could be expected from it?
It may call itself the Cold Truth, the End of All—
But in the end, the pain its destruction causes is no different than the pain the new Shadows that have emerged have caused."
Seraphielle declared coldly, but then, she extended her hand. The halo behind her spun faster, scattering light in all directions.
"And yet, even now, I do not hate any of it."
She spoke, her voice once again became soft.
"For everything in this Universe is still part of what was created.
Light exists not to erase everything—
But to remind it what it has forgotten and bring the Order that our Universe needs."
She announced.
"And to do this—
The Chain Breakers will be the first step Light takes.
To all life that still breathes within the embrace of the cosmos—
Do not fear the coming storm.
Do not bow to those who claim dominion through shadow.
Because the Light has not yet died.
The Light will shine again—
And this time, it will be brighter than ever."

sentences.text: "The guilty did not repent.
The cruel did not reflect.
And the Shadows—
The Shadows have forgotten their place."
Those words echoed throughout the Universe, heard by every single being, be it in the Faction of Light, Darkness, Eternity, or Balance.

Even those who weren’t directly or even indirectly linked with any of these Factions—even those who were learning of the very existence of the Supreme World of Light for the first time—heard her voice.
The golden radiance that carried her words still rippled through the cosmos.
Worlds glowed like stars, suns dimmed before her light, and even the void itself seemed to shimmer, unable to reject her presence.
In every corner of existence—be it worlds of flame, oceans of mist, or the frozen cities drifting through eternity—they all felt her presence.
It... it felt like the Universe itself was allowing it to happen.
"My children,"
Seraphielle spoke again.
"The storm you feel... is not the end.
It is but a ripple—a shadow’s last cry before it fades."
Her words carried heavy, commanding warmth.
A contradiction in itself, it was like... the warm, comfortable embrace of sunlight that was too bright to endure.
"Their challenge, their blasphemy... was not made against you.
It was made against us—against the Light that has guided all life since the first spark."
Seraphielle’s gaze drifted beyond the temple, as if she could see the countless beings who were awed by her presence.
"They believe themselves free because theybroke the chainsthey imagined.
But tell me—
What freedom is born from defiance of order?
What strength lies in hatred of the hand that protects?"
Her vast and radiant wings unfurled.
"They call themselves Chain Breakers.
And yet, in breaking what binds, they have only shattered what shields.
They have brought not liberty—but chaos.
They have not defied darkness—they have become it."
Her golden aura pulsed outward again, strengthening around the entire Universe as every being felt even closer to her.
Almost as if... it was inescapable.
"I will not allow it."
She declared, her voice carried absolute authority, as if her words alone were more than enough to stop everything that had happened.
Even the Universe’s anger seemed to have calmed down ever since she released her aura.
This was also the reason the Universe was actively supporting her to spread her message.
And Seraphielle had no intention of letting this chance go.
"The Light does not abandon its creation.
It has not done so in the past—
It will not do so now."
Across millions of worlds, people fell silent, listening to her words intensely.
After everything that had happened, after how the Universe’s constant angry fits left most of them in shambles, desperate for help, these words became... hope.
This was... such a strong display of power and authority that even the proudest Eternals lowered their heads.
This was not the speech of a ruler—it was... the declaration of existence itself.
Seraphielle raised her hand slightly, and the radiance grew warmer.
"For eons, I trusted Balance.
I trusted the others to keep their promise—to guard this Universe as we once swore together."
Her words flowed gently.
She didn’t accuse anyone, she didn’t blame anyone—or at least, that was the illusion her tone and gentleness created.
"Balance, however, is now broken."
But deep down—her words were sharper than any blade.
"It claims neutrality and calls it peace.
But peace without action is decay.
It watched as the scales tilted and called it equilibrium.
It watched as the innocent bled and called it destiny."
She paused for a slight moment, letting her words sink in before—
"The Universe does not need watchers.
It needs guardians."
She declared, her voice filled with reassurance.
But the Infinity of Light wasn’t yet done—
"Then comes Eternity.
It dwells in the archives of forever, studying what has been and what will be.
Its wisdom is indeed unmatched, yet...
In search for meaning,
It forgot... compassion."
She spoke, her tone carried no anger, only disappointment so profound that even the Eternity Borns trembled and lowered their heads in guilt.
"The Universe doesn’t need scholars to know it all.
It does not need scholars who scavenge through historic records and predict billions of unpredictable future possibilities—
It needs beings who learn from history and prevent the same mistakes from happening again.
It needs beings who stand when the very existence of the Universe is under threat."
The Infinity of Light muttered.
Her words earned trillions and trillions of nods.
Her ideas of compassion and mercy began to spread, and now, when the time was most optimal—
"And Darkness..."
She breathed, her tone shifting for the first time.
She was still calm, but this time, it was filled with judgment.
"It disappointed me the least."
She began—her words contrary to what the Darkness Borns were expecting to hear.
But then—
"What was born from silence and death, what thrives in destruction, death, and wars, what spreads fear and names it power—what else could be expected from it?
It may call itself the Cold Truth, the End of All—
But in the end, the pain its destruction causes is no different than the pain the new Shadows that have emerged have caused."
Seraphielle declared coldly, but then, she extended her hand.
The halo behind her spun faster, scattering light in all directions.
"And yet, even now, I do not hate any of it."
She spoke, her voice once again became soft.
"For everything in this Universe is still part of what was created.
Light exists not to erase everything—
But to remind it what it has forgotten and bring the Order that our Universe needs."
She announced.
"And to do this—
The Chain Breakers will be the first step Light takes.
To all life that still breathes within the embrace of the cosmos—
Do not fear the coming storm.
Do not bow to those who claim dominion through shadow.
Because the Light has not yet died.
The Light will shine again—
And this time, it will be brighter than ever."

chapters.title: Chapter 2166: Could it be that we… died?
paragraphs: Inside a silent, empty yet infinite void, more than a hundred beings with long golden wings and bright golden light around them hovered in silence. From afar, their appearance was in complete contrast with their dark surroundings. In this dark space, they looked like a sea of suns, releasing endless, blinding light.
Their halos shimmered, wings of crystal light unfurled behind them, spreading waves of gold and white brilliance across the abyss.
Every single one of them had an Aura beyond what most people in the entirety of the Universe would be able to stand against.
Yes, they were all Eternals.
Beings who had lived for billions of years, fought wars older than most worlds, and... ruled beings until they got tired of it.
That was who they were.
The Light Borns.

However, as these beings—who most people thought of as legends—looked around, frowns appeared on their Divine Faces. Even though they could see that they were in a dimension similar to the Universe they came from, something felt... wrong—oddly unnerving.
This place might seem like the Universe they were familiar with, but at the same time... it was... not?
All of them looked around, confused. The flow of Laws and Energy felt the same, but... the pulse—the rhythm of existence—it was different.
It felt... cold.
It felt... detached.
As if they were inside something that... only pretended to be real.
"Where... are we...?"
One of the Light Borns questioned, his eyes still looking around carefully.
"Lord Light brought me here..."
Another answered.

She was investigating a Middle-Level World that seemed to have an oddly close connection with one of the High-Level Worlds that had disappeared in a recent Anomaly’s attack, but as she continued, she suddenly felt her body being forcefully pulled out of one space and teleported to another.
A power only Lord Light held over them.
"Me too."
Another Light Born nodded. Like the woman, he too felt the pull. One by one, everyone began to nod. It was clear that Lord Light was the one who brought them here.
"But... if he was the only one who summoned us...
Then... where is he?"
Another Light Born asked as he continued looking around, searching for Lord Light.
"You do not get to question his decision."
Suddenly, another Light Born spoke with a solemn look on his face.
"If he sent us here, he must have a reason."
More Light Borns nodded at those words, but then suddenly—
Another Light Born spoke with a stutter, an action that surprised all the others since none of them ever expected one of their kind to... stutter.
"Aadayan?"
The first Light Born tilted her head, a little confused.
"Are you alright?"
She asked, and the Light Born named Aadayan shook his head with a solemn look on his face, making the woman frown.
"What happened? Why are you acting like that?"

At her words, Aadayan massaged his temples. His head felt like it would burst apart any moment now. The rest of the Light Borns didn’t rush him either, giving him all the time he wanted, but Aadayan knew that, unlike how the rest of them thought...
They...
They did not have time.
"I... I saw the Anomaly."
Aadayan revealed, and in an instant, the expressions of the other Light Borns changed.
"You saw... the Anomaly?
What did you do then?
Did you fight against him?
How did the battle end? How strong was he? Was he a challenge at all? Did he have any interesting abilities? Did—"
One of them asked a series of questions, and he wanted to ask more but—
"I reported to Lord Light the moment I saw him."
Aadayan cut him off.
"What did he say...?"
Another Light Born questioned. He did not like the heavy, grim tone in Aadayan’s voice. It felt like something was about to happen—something they were not prepared for.

"He took over my body to see him himself. I thought he would face the enemy, but instead, he released the control over my body in order to return to the temple, moved all of you next to me, and then took over my body again."
He explained, and the others around him—with billions of years of experience in their heads—could instantly understand what Aadayan was trying to say.
"So the Lord wanted us to attack him together."
One spoke, and Aadayan nodded at those words.
"Wait a minute."
But another Light Born frowned again.
"You said... Lord Light took over your body, then... how come you are yourself?
Did he release his control over your body?"
"More than release his control... it felt like... he was pushed out of my body, forcefully."
Aadayan replied, and in an instant, the Light Borns around him blinked in disbelief.
"What are you talking about? Force Lord Light out of your body? You should know better than others that this isn’t possible.
The bond Lord Light has with us is far stronger than anything most beings could even imagine. Breaking that connection is absolutely impossible—"
Or at least...
That was what he thought, but then suddenly—
"I... I can no longer connect with Lord Light..."
Another Light Born muttered out loud, his voice filled with disbelief.
"What...?"
The other Light Borns frowned. The next instant, they all tried to connect with Lord Light through the Communication Orb but...
They all failed.
Their connection... seemed to have disappeared.
"...What is happening?"
A Light Born muttered.
"How can I not sense... Lord Light’s presence...?
Did... did something happen to him?"
"Have you lost your mind?"
His words were instantly discarded.
What could possibly happen to Lord Light? The power he held was absolute. If anything were to happen, it wouldn’t be to him but to...
The moment he thought about it, the Light Born’s expression changed.
"Wait..."
He called out, staring at Aadayan.
"You said you saw the Anomaly...
Where is he?"
He asked, and his question instantly made all the other Light Borns silent.
And Aadayan...
"I... I do not know."
He shook his head.
"We are not in the place I was.
We...
It seems like we were teleported again before our connection with Lord Light was snapped."
"Just what are you even saying? We were teleported and we didn’t even feel anything?"
"I... I saw some dark light surround me before I woke up... could it be that?"
Another Light Born suggested until finally—
"Could it be...
Could it be that we... died?"

chapters.title: Chapter 2167: Enough of your celestial poetry.
paragraphs: "Could it be...
Could it be that we... died?"
One of the Light Borns spoke, his voice cracking as he looked around. As these words came out of his mouth, this place now felt even eerier.

Generally, they could talk to Lord Light no matter where they were, be it another World or even the void where most communication fails. In their long lives, there had never been a moment where they couldn’t connect to Lord Light. After all, their very lives were connected to Lord Light, allowing them to contact him any time they wanted— all Light Borns knew that.
But what if...
The life that connects them with Lord Light... no longer exists?
He wondered in his head.
Not to mention, before coming here, they were about to face the Anomaly, were they not? What if... they did have a battle and what if... they were defeated...?
Then the question arises—why doesn’t any of them remember it? And there could be many answers to that.
Maybe the Anomaly messed with their minds before the battle ended?

That was very much a possibility. From their investigations, and seeing how even after spending a few hours, they failed to find even a single clue that connected everything to the enemy, it was clear that the enemy was used to manipulating memories.
There was no way none of them would remember him otherwise.
But...
If they truly died...
Then...
"Does this mean this place is an afterlife...?"
The Light Born muttered.

According to what they were told, an afterlife did not exist. In the Universe, if a being dies, his Soul enters the Cycle of Reincarnation, where it is cleansed of the past life it had lived and is reincarnated again in another World.
But...
What if... that was untrue...?
And even if it was true...
What if this place was the Cycle of Reincarnation? A place where they would be ’cleansed’ before finally losing themselves?
The moment he thought about it, his body trembled.
And it wasn’t just him. With the influence of his words, the other Light Borns around him could feel the same.
"We... were defeated...? All of us...?"
"But... wasn’t Lord Light with us? Didn’t he possess Aadayan’s body? How could we... lose when he was beside us?"
"What if... Lord Light lost as well...?"
Aadayan muttered after a slight hesitation and in an instant—
"Aadayan!"
"Preposterous!"
"Blasphemy!"
The Light Borns reacted strongly, not even entertaining that idea. Their Lord was absolute. How could he, an Infinity, possibly lose against an enemy they didn’t even know about a few centuries ago?
But Aadayan hadn’t said those words without thinking...
"We... lost when our Lord was with us!
We are in the Afterlife, or inside the Cycle of Reincarnation!
What other explain—"
"Afterlife? Cycle of Reincarnation?
You guys sure have strong imagination."

Before Aadayan could complete his words, a voice full of mockery was heard. In an instant, all the Light Borns turned, staring at the being who had appeared in front of them, and the moment they saw him, their expressions changed.
They...
They knew who he was.
The Anomaly.
In an instant, the Light Borns’ faces turned grim. The Anomaly, however, was different—he just grinned at them and then shrugged,
"But then again, thinking about it from a certain perspective, your guesses aren’t entirely wrong either.
In some way, you can think of this place as the afterlife or the cycle of reincarnation, yes."
The Light Borns narrowed their eyes at his words. Aadayan carefully stepped forward and—
"If you are here... then doesn’t it mean...?"
"What else would it mean? Lord Light must have squashed him like the bug he is. This battle between the Anomaly and the Supreme Worlds is over."
Another Light Born snorted with a grin full of contempt.
Nux, hearing those words, blinked, raising his eyebrows in disbelief.
Just... just how brainwashed were these people?
Do they... truly even consider the possibility of their Lord losing?
Is this... the result of standing at the very top since time immemorial?
Nux thought all this. The Light Borns, however, were oblivious to what he was thinking and continued showing their disdain.
"To think he and his people made such a fuss about—what was that? Breaking the chains?"

"It was something about how our rule will rot, influence will burn, and how our name will no longer command fear. Their little group sure did come up with bold words. It was entertaining to say the very least."
The Light Borns laughed.
"But why is it just him...?"
Another Light Born frowned.
"Where’s the rest? Even if I have fallen in the battle, I would still like to see everyone responsible for entertaining me during the last moments of my life."
"Who knows? Maybe Lord Light has... other uses for them."
A Light Born spoke, his eyes shining with a cruel glint—something that Nux found quite amusing.
"Don’t you people represent love and peace or some bullshit like that?
Should you be saying such words?"
He asked curiously.
"As if that matters anymore."
The Light Born shrugged.
"Leave him be. I am having a hard time understanding how he managed to come here so quickly. With the things he has done, an end like this one... doesn’t it seem... too easy for him?"
"Indeed."
"Our Lord Light is merciful; maybe he showed mercy."
Another Light Born spoke, but the rest waved their hands in dismissal.
"We are no longer connected to him or the Supreme World of Light. We no longer need the Energy of Light. Do you not sense it?
Our connection with him no longer exists. He cannot hear us; we can freely speak our minds here.
Merciful?
That being?
Stop playing into his hypocritical theatrics even after your death."
"Indeed, there is no need for us to do this anymore."
Another Light Born nodded.
Then one of them stretched his body and—
"Heh, hypocritical bastard."
He cursed.
"I had hoped I could see his death with my own eyes, but I guess he is too strong for that, huh..."
"Indeed, indeed."
The rest of the Light Borns nodded.
Nux, who was hearing those words, raised his eyebrow in amusement.
Then suddenly, another one of them stretched his body before looking in a certain direction and—
"How odd."
He laughed.
"To think we, hailed as few of the strongest beings in the entire Universe, are only able to speak our minds when we have fallen.
Maybe it is true.
Death is the only freedom one can seek."
The rest of the Light Borns nodded at those words, each adding their own perspective to his words until finally—
"Will you stop with whatever this philosophical bullshit you have come up with?
Enough of your celestial poetry.
I have things I want you lot to do,
So start being useful before I lose my mind."
Nux snapped.

"Indeed, there is no need for us to do this anymore."
Another Light Born nodded.
Then one of them stretched his body and—
"Heh, hypocritical bastard."
He cursed.
"I had hoped I could see his death with my own eyes, but I guess he is too strong for that, huh..."
"Indeed, indeed."
The rest of the Light Borns nodded.
Nux, who was hearing those words, raised his eyebrow in amusement.
Then suddenly, another one of them stretched his body before looking in a certain direction and—
"How odd."
He laughed.
"To think we, hailed as few of the strongest beings in the entire Universe, are only able to speak our minds when we have fallen.
Maybe it is true.
Death is the only freedom one can seek."
The rest of the Light Borns nodded at those words, each adding their own perspective to his words until finally—
"Will you stop with whatever this philosophical bullshit you have come up with?
Enough of your celestial poetry.
I have things I want you lot to do,
So start being useful before I lose my mind."
Nux snapped.

chapters.title: Chapter 2168: What are you doing?
paragraphs: "Will you stop with whatever this philosophical bullshit you have come up with?
Enough of your celestial poetry.
I have things I want you lot to do,
So start being useful before I lose my mind."
Nux snapped, staring at the Light Borns with an annoyed look on his face.
And the Light Borns...
They stared back at him in silence.
For a few seconds, the entire dark void turned silent, only the golden light that the Light Borns released broke that empty darkness.
Then finally—
"Things you want us to do?"
One of them laughed coldly.
"What do you even mean by that?"
Another Light Born scoffed, his golden eyes narrowing.
"Why would we ever do what you say?"
Another asked.
"You think you can order us around just because we’ve fallen?"
"Don’t mistake us for your allies, Anomaly."
Another stepped forward and spoke with a cold look on his face.
"And lose your mind? What if youdolose your mind? What then? What are you going to do? You’re dead. Just like us. You think your grand title scares us?"
"You are dead, just like us.
There is nothing scary about you anymore, Anomaly.
If anything,
You are a failure.
One who failed to fulfil his words—a waste.
An arrogant fool."
Their voices overlapped—their mockery, their defiance, their anger. They didn’t hide any of these ’negative’ emotions in their voices.
The noble calmness and gentleness they once carried were nowhere to be seen. After all, they had already died.
They were no longer holy beings of ’order and grace’—right now, they were merely bitter remnants of what they used to be.
Free remnants who could do and speak what they wanted, without any other being constantly watching over them.
As the Light Borns snapped back at him, Nux stared at them with a blank expression. There was no anger or frustration in his eyes, it was just... disappointment.
For a moment, he considered talking to them, explaining that unlike what they believed, they weren’t actually dead but...
Seeing their expressions—those arrogant, despising smiles, the body language that screamed that they no longer cared about the consequences of their actions anymore...
It was clear that it wouldn’t work, and even if it did, he would need a lot of time to actually convince these arrogant fools—
"Forget it."
He sighed as he rubbed the back of his neck, then, he stared at the group of golden lights in front of him and then—
Then he moved.
BOOM
With just a single movement, he dashed forward, faster than any of the Light Borns could react to—even then, they all prepared themselves for whatever was about to happen.
But...
Nothing happened...
The Light Borns looked around, trying to find where Nux was. As for Nux...
He stood a little further away with a frown on his face.𝚏𝗿𝗲𝐞𝐰𝚎𝕓𝐧𝚘𝘃𝗲𝐥.𝐜𝚘𝕞
He...
He had missed.
He appeared several meters away from where he had aimed. His movements were too fast, too strong, too... unbalanced.
Yes.
It had happened again.

He had devoured a total of fifteen High-Level Worlds, and because this time he devoured complete worlds—together with their Wills and all life in them—the strength he gained from them was twice what he would usually get.
Currently, his physical body was nearly thirty times stronger than what it was before.
And he...
He had no control over it.
He looked at his own hands and sighed again.
"Tch... I hate this feeling..."
He clicked his tongue in annoyance.
Soon, however, he exhaled deeply and sighed again. Then he stared at the light bulbs in front of him and convinced himself.
He didn’t need to feel frustrated—he knew the problem, and this was the reason he was here in the first place.
More than a hundred Eternals, and not just any Eternals—Eternals who were said to be the strongest of all Eternals—they were more than enough to help him adapt, were they not?
Yes, this was the ’use’ Nux had for them.
In the end, he stared at the training dummies in front of him and his figure blurred again. The second time, he moved with better control.
And this time—
He managed to grab one—not the one he had intended, but since he had chosen the area with a relatively higher number of training dummies, he managed to grab one that was most convenient.
"Wha—!"
The captured Light Born’s golden aura flared instantly, his wings spreading wide as he struggled.
But...
With Nux grabbing his head, no matter what he did, no matter how strongly he struggled, it was useless.
Then suddenly—
WFHOOSH
A dark, heavy energy surged from Nux’s body, spilling into the air like liquid shadow. It wrapped itself around the struggling Eternal, smothering his light completely.
"W-What is this!?"

The Light Born screamed, trying to break free. His golden arms trembled, energy burned through his veins as he used all his power to break free. His wings constantly flapped in the air, trying to push his body away from this monstrosity, but just like before, no matter how much power he used, no matter what he did, Nux’s grip didn’t even shake.
"Stop it!"
Another Light Born shouted.
"Have you lost your mind!?"
A few of them dashed forward, their wings slicing through the darkness, their Auras flaring up, preparing to attack and slice Nux’s body in half—
But Nux moved again and disappeared—
He reappeared far away, still holding the struggling Light Born in one hand.
The rest of the Light Borns stopped mid-flight. The distance between them had widened; they were scared that if they moved too boldly, he might do something.
Instead—they tried to talk—
"What are you doing?"
One of them questioned with a solemn look on his face.
But Nux...

He just stared without any change in his expression. The Light Born he was holding wasn’t even visible. The other Light Borns could tell he was still struggling to break free, but the monster holding him was... strong—too strong.
And then, the Light Borns noticed something.
The black energy that had surrounded their comrade began to fade away. They all waited, but as the black energy faded completely—
Their comrade... had faded out of existence as well.

chapters.title: Chapter 2169: That felt itchy.
paragraphs: The black energy that had surrounded their comrade began to fade away. They all waited, but as the black energy faded completely—
Their comrade... had faded out of existence as well.
His Aura, the Golden Energy he released, their connection to him—it all... vanished.
And what was left was...
Silence.
The remaining Light Borns froze, their glowing eyes widened.
"What... what did you do to him...?"
One of them whispered.
Nux, who was staring at his hand, slowly turned to them, and a faint grin appeared on his face.
"Do you finally realize it now...?"
He spoke in a soft, calm, but chilling voice.
"This is not the Afterlife, nor is this the Cycle of Reincarnation—
None of you are dead.
You are very much alive."
He revealed.
"What...?"
The Light Borns stiffened, their auras flickering in disbelief.
Nux’s grin widened, twisting into something demonic. His golden eyes burned brighter—but the golden shade in his eyes was different compared to the Light Borns’.
His eyes did not reflect holiness or grace...
His eyes showed hunger.
A predatory hunger prepared to devour it all.
"But don’t worry,"
He spoke in a low, almost playful voice.
"I’ve prepared a fate far worse than death for you."
Before they could react, he vanished again. Once more, his hand grabbed another Light Born, and the same dark energy wrapped itself around him.
Again, the Light Born screamed, he struggled, just like the one before him did, but... the result was no different.
Another light disappeared into the void.
And this time, the Light Borns felt it—
This time, they felt it—the dangerous, devouring force that threatened their very sense of existence...
The Light Borns stared at the monster in front of them—and finally, realization dawned.
The Anomaly—he wasn’t lying, nor was he trying to trick them.
This wasn’t the end.
This wasn’t the afterlife.
This was... the beginning—
The beginning of their battle against the Anomaly.
The Light Borns stared at each other, their Auras flaring brightly as they all nodded, preparing themselves for the battle ahead.
Once again, the Light Borns stared at the being in front of them, their expressions now different from before.
It was about to begin.
The battle between the Golden Light and the Endless Darkness—
And Nux...
He grinned as he moved forward.
But this time, the Light Borns didn’t just let him do what he wanted—
BOOOOOM
This time, they released their Auras strongly. More than a hundred Light Borns released their energies at the same time, trying to suppress the enemy with their Aura. And this wasn’t all—
The group had prepared something else too.

At the same time, all hundred Light Borns released their Domains. The goal was simple—suppress the enemy’s Domain with theirs, and once the Anomaly was inside their Domain—the battle was as good as over.
Or at least... that was what the Light Borns believed, but...
The moment they activated their Domains—or tried to—they realized something.
Their Domains...
They could not release them.
While their Laws still worked, they... for some reason, couldn’t extend them to Domains...
"What...?"
One of the Light Borns muttered aloud, his eyes widening in disbelief.
"I... I cannot release my Domain..."
Another muttered.
"Me neither..."
The rest of the Light Borns faced the same problem. A wave of confusion spread through the place, the Light Borns staring at each other in disbelief—but suddenly—
"Let me GO!"
A shout was heard.
The Light Borns turned toward the sound and saw another one of their comrades in the enemy’s hand, struggling with everything he had. The same black energy surrounded him—
As for the enemy...
He stared at them and—
"Oh right, I think I forgot to tell you."
He began, as if he had just remembered.
"This isn’t the Afterlife or the Cycle of Reincarnation—but that doesn’t mean this place isn’t special—"
He smiled. The Light Borns narrowed their eyes at those words, and he—
"You cannot use your Domains here."
Nux revealed with an innocent smile as the black energy he released faded again, taking another one of their comrades with it.
And Nux’s grin widened—
"So you, my friends, are on your own.
I wish you the best of luck."
The Light Borns clenched their fists in anger and frustration. Seeing the clear disdain and mockery in Nux’s eyes made their bodies tremble.
He was openly provoking them.
And he...
He would pay the price for that—
"Spread formation,"
One of them ordered, and without wasting any time, the hundred and one Light Borns left got into formation, forming concentric rings of radiance that instantly surrounded the enemy.
Their Auras flared again, their bodies burning with endless energy, and in perfect synchronization, they moved.
"Solar Dominion: Nova Bloom!"

The Leader of the Formation announced, and the rest moved accordingly. They had used the same formation so many times that it was instilled into their very bodies—it was next to impossible to make a mistake.
The dark void exploded into gold.
BOOOOOOOOOM
Hundreds of miniature suns detonated around Nux, the energy tearing space apart, reducing everything within range to molten particles of light.
The explosions were so bright that even time itself seemed to stutter.
An attack capable of wiping out even the strongest beings out of existence, an attack that Nux couldn’t possibly escape since he was caught right in the middle of it—
It was over.
So quickly that honestly, the Light Borns were taken aback—
"Wasn’t it... too easy...?"
One of them said aloud.
"So much for—"
Another one wanted to nod with a grin but...
But when the light faded...
Every single Light Born could see it—a faint figure that became clearer and clearer.
"What...?"
One of them muttered, his mouth agape.
"He... survived...?"
"But... how...?"
None could believe it.
He was there.
Standing still—untouched.
No injuries, no bruises...
The combined attack of a hundred Eternal-Level Light Borns... did absolutely nothing to him. And as if he were trying to rub it in—
Nux scratched his arm with a somewhat annoyed look on his face and—
"That felt itchy."
He then stared at the Light Borns and frowned—
"But wasn’t it too much work just for a mere light show?"
