chapters.title: Chapter 2170: He… he’s fast—!
paragraphs: "That felt itchy."
Nux spoke as he scratched his elbow with a slightly uncomfortable look on his face before glancing at the Light Borns in confusion and—
"But wasn’t it too much work just for a mere light show?"
"...what?"
"...Light show...?"
The Light Borns couldn’t believe what they were seeing.

The golden flames that should have burned him to ashes danced around his skin harmlessly before fading into nothing. The Light Borns looked at the man hovering in front of them carefully, trying to find something—anything.
But...
Nothing.
There was nothing.
Their attack... it did absolutely no damage.
And it wasn’t regeneration. The Anomaly didn’t regenerate or heal his injuries after being harmed, he just...
Their attack just... did not work. His body’s raw defense was... that strong.
T-That can’t be!"
One of the Light Borns spoke.
"T-This must be one of his tricks! His abilities!

There were reports of him having Power of Space, were there not? He must have used some Space Law to transfer the impact of our attack to some other space! This is the reason he himself is unaffected!"
He theorized.
A theory that would have normally worked and been quite believable but...
They were the Light Borns.

These beings had ruled over others as the strongest for trillions of years. Their combined attack... if its damage could possibly be ’teleported’ to some other space like the Light Born said—they wouldn’t hold the title of one of the strongest.

Their attack did true damage through light itself. Even if the enemy had the ability to transfer the impact of an attack somewhere else, he would need to react at the speed of light and use his ability at the exact moment for it to work—
A task which was simply impossible, especially against an attack as grand as Nova Bloom, which did damage and changed its pattern at every single instance.
There was absolutely no way an enemy could avoid this attack unless he teleported himself and dodged the attack entirely but...
That was clearly not the case here.
Not that the Light Borns believed it—they were sure. The Anomaly was trying to fool them. He must have teleported away and reappeared when the attack was bearable.
There was no way he could take their attack head-on otherwise.
Of course, Nux had no idea what they were thinking, neither did he care. He just tilted his head slightly, feeling his muscles tighten accordingly as if he was studying his own body.
Then—
He moved and—
BOOOOOM
In an instant, a shockwave rippled through the void.
One instant, he was standing still, the second, he appeared right in front of one Light Born, his fist already buried in his chest.
"What...?"

The Eternal’s radiant armor shattered like glass. The Light Born stared at the monstrosity standing in front of him with a horrified look on his face as golden blood dripped down from his agape mouth.
In shock, he looked down and realized there was a big hole in his chest. His golden blood flowed without stopping while his body began to heal but—
The familiar dark energy quickly surrounded him. He tried to move or resist, but his body was busy healing the fatal wound it had just suffered. He had no strength to move.
In the end, the Light Born lost his vision. The black energy surrounded him completely, the last thing he heard was—
"He... he’s fast—!"
"A-Attack him!"
His comrades rushing towards him gave him a sense of relief, but honestly, deep inside, he could feel it as well.
This... was the end.
Even if his comrades gave their all, this wasn’t a battle they could win.
He... he couldn’t be saved.
And he was right.
"C-Charge!"
The Light Borns rushed towards Nux. His body twisted in reaction, his leg sweeping through the void, colliding with another Light Born.
BOOOOM

With just one attack, the said Light Born was sent flying back, coughing blood while the bones inside his body shattered in a way that even someone like him, who could heal any wound within seconds, would need more than a few minutes to recover.
Another Light Born tried to block Nux with his sword, but Nux’s kick tore through the shield, bent his arm, and sent him crashing into the void, his halo flickering violently.
The shockwaves every single one of his movements created warped the very space around them. It was clear—even this space itself couldn’t take how ridiculously strong this monster was.
The Light Borns, however, noticed something.
Nux’s breathing was... uneven.
He hadn’t even moved much, but it felt like he was already tired. No, he didn’t look tired—it was something else.
His movements seemed... rough, unrefined... one that hadn’t developed yet.
Then suddenly—
"Wait... it happened before...
He tried to move and appeared in a completely different place...
Was that... a mistake?"
One of them pointed out.
And soon, the Light Borns realized it.
The enemy...
He was strong, yes, but...
He wasn’t undefeatable.
"Change formation!
Engage from all sides!"
And just then, with a reformed hope in their hearts, another order was passed. The Light Borns moved. Thirty of them raised their arms, their halos merging to form a massive ring of light.
Whoosh Whoosh Whoosh
Inside it, thousands of Light Sigils began to spin, creating a colossal, ever-turning sun.
"Cathedral Manifestation!"

The ring expanded, birthing radiant towers of energy that surrounded Nux, locking him in a divine fortress of light that sealed the Space Laws itself. Spears of condensed golden light rained down from every direction, each carrying the power to erase mountains, worlds, even souls.
But Nux...
He just let it happen.
He let the golden rain fall on him, his body moving as he dodged them one by one. A decision the Light Borns grinned at.
After all, they had all seen that the enemy’s body wasn’t properly coordinated—
Dodging thousands of spears in a limited space...
It was... impossible.
And they were right.
Nux barely dodged about eighteen spears until finally, he moved a little too much to the left and one of the spears landed right on his chest—
BOOOOOOOM

sentences.text: "That felt itchy."
Nux spoke as he scratched his elbow with a slightly uncomfortable look on his face before glancing at the Light Borns in confusion and—
"But wasn’t it too much work just for a mere light show?"
"...what?"
"...Light show...?"
The Light Borns couldn’t believe what they were seeing.
The golden flames that should have burned him to ashes danced around his skin harmlessly before fading into nothing.
The Light Borns looked at the man hovering in front of them carefully, trying to find something—anything.
But...
Nothing.
There was nothing.
Their attack... it did absolutely no damage.
And it wasn’t regeneration.
The Anomaly didn’t regenerate or heal his injuries after being harmed, he just...
Their attack just... did not work.
His body’s raw defense was... that strong.
T-That can’t be!"
One of the Light Borns spoke.
"T-This must be one of his tricks!
His abilities!
There were reports of him having Power of Space, were there not?
He must have used some Space Law to transfer the impact of our attack to some other space!
This is the reason he himself is unaffected!"
He theorized.
A theory that would have normally worked and been quite believable but...
They were the Light Borns.
These beings had ruled over others as the strongest for trillions of years.
Their combined attack... if its damage could possibly be ’teleported’ to some other space like the Light Born said—they wouldn’t hold the title of one of the strongest.
Their attack did true damage through light itself.
Even if the enemy had the ability to transfer the impact of an attack somewhere else, he would need to react at the speed of light and use his ability at the exact moment for it to work—
A task which was simply impossible, especially against an attack as grand as Nova Bloom, which did damage and changed its pattern at every single instance.
There was absolutely no way an enemy could avoid this attack unless he teleported himself and dodged the attack entirely but...
That was clearly not the case here.
Not that the Light Borns believed it—they were sure.
The Anomaly was trying to fool them.
He must have teleported away and reappeared when the attack was bearable.
There was no way he could take their attack head-on otherwise.
Of course, Nux had no idea what they were thinking, neither did he care.
He just tilted his head slightly, feeling his muscles tighten accordingly as if he was studying his own body.
Then—
He moved and—
BOOOOOM
In an instant, a shockwave rippled through the void.
One instant, he was standing still, the second, he appeared right in front of one Light Born, his fist already buried in his chest.
"What...?"
The Eternal’s radiant armor shattered like glass.
The Light Born stared at the monstrosity standing in front of him with a horrified look on his face as golden blood dripped down from his agape mouth.
In shock, he looked down and realized there was a big hole in his chest.
His golden blood flowed without stopping while his body began to heal but—
The familiar dark energy quickly surrounded him.
He tried to move or resist, but his body was busy healing the fatal wound it had just suffered.
He had no strength to move.
In the end, the Light Born lost his vision.
The black energy surrounded him completely, the last thing he heard was—
"He... he’s fast—!"
"A-Attack him!"
His comrades rushing towards him gave him a sense of relief, but honestly, deep inside, he could feel it as well.
This... was the end.
Even if his comrades gave their all, this wasn’t a battle they could win.
He... he couldn’t be saved.
And he was right.
"C-Charge!"
The Light Borns rushed towards Nux.
His body twisted in reaction, his leg sweeping through the void, colliding with another Light Born.
BOOOOM

With just one attack, the said Light Born was sent flying back, coughing blood while the bones inside his body shattered in a way that even someone like him, who could heal any wound within seconds, would need more than a few minutes to recover.
Another Light Born tried to block Nux with his sword, but Nux’s kick tore through the shield, bent his arm, and sent him crashing into the void, his halo flickering violently.
The shockwaves every single one of his movements created warped the very space around them.
It was clear—even this space itself couldn’t take how ridiculously strong this monster was.
The Light Borns, however, noticed something.
Nux’s breathing was... uneven.
He hadn’t even moved much, but it felt like he was already tired.
No, he didn’t look tired—it was something else.
His movements seemed... rough, unrefined... one that hadn’t developed yet.
Then suddenly—
"Wait... it happened before...
He tried to move and appeared in a completely different place...
Was that... a mistake?"
One of them pointed out.
And soon, the Light Borns realized it.
The enemy...
He was strong, yes, but...
He wasn’t undefeatable.
"Change formation!
Engage from all sides!"
And just then, with a reformed hope in their hearts, another order was passed.
The Light Borns moved.

Whoosh Whoosh Whoosh

chapters.title: Chapter 2171: Come on now. Don’t give in.
paragraphs: Nux moved, dodging the incoming golden spears one by one. His movements were by no means graceful or effortless; in fact, one could see how much he had to focus just to avoid getting attacked. Actually, the only reason he was even able to manage and dodge all the spears was because his body was ridiculously fast.
Even if he moved at the very last instant, his body helped him fill in the gaps and dodge the spear successfully.
But since every single one of his movements was so extreme, every time he moved, he lost some sense of balance.

However, this didn’t stop him. If anything, it only pushed him even further. He forced his body to regain his balance and continued. His rough movements began to improve at a ridiculous pace, as if he had done the same thing hundreds of thousands of times. His rhythm and body coordination continued to improve.
He was learning—adapting—in real time.
So quickly that even the Light Borns who were watching him ’struggle’ couldn’t help but notice his change. But just before they were about to panic and release another wave of attack—

One of the spears moved past Nux’s defenses. He dodged at the very last instant, throwing himself backward, but unfortunately, another spear appeared right where he landed and this time, it hit his chest—
BOOOOOOOM
A huge explosion was heard, engulfing Nux.
The Light Borns grinned, some clenching their fists, celebrating the successful attack.

After all, this time, they had seen with their own eyes that their attack had landed right in front of them. There was no way the enemy would be able to take an attack at such a level head-on and come out without grievous injuries.
Now, all they needed to do was to prepare for the next phase of the battle, where they would try to capture the injured Anomaly.
"Don’t kill him.
He will be useful."
One of them ordered. Others, who thought the same, nodded as they took their battle stance, ready for the final phase.𝘧𝑟𝑒𝑒𝘸𝘦𝘣𝑛𝑜𝘷𝑒𝓁.𝘤𝘰𝓂
But then...
A familiar scene replayed.
As the bright light faded away, a figure appeared, and the Light Borns... they all once again widened their eyes in horror.
Yes, once again, the Anomaly was unhurt.
This time, he didn’t even look annoyed—he seemed... disappointed.
"Just eighteen, huh...
I have definitely lost my touch."
He nodded to himself before he closed his eyes and sighed—
"Whatever, I still have time—"
His gaze then fell on the Light Borns and—
"—and the training dummies. I can do it."
He nodded to himself, his eyes regaining their light.
The Light Borns, however, were different.
"H-He survived!!"
One of them shouted, bringing others out of their reverie.
"H-How!?"
Questions were asked.
Questions no one had the answers to.
"Alright, try doing that again.
I want to see if I reach a higher number this time."
Nux muttered with a grin.
To him, this was never a battle to begin with. This was... this was just another training session.
His words only worked to offend the Light Borns. Their eyes flared with anger as one of them raised his hand—
"Conversion!"
He announced as he clenched his fists.
Whoosh Whoosh Whoosh

Hundreds of radiant symbols formed in the air. The Light Borns poured their collective energies into one single strike—a golden beam as thick as a world’s core, forged from the prayers of a thousand galaxies.
Everything happened so quickly that within a second, the attack was ready, and without wasting any time, the Light Borns pointed toward Nux.
Nux wanted to dodge it, so he prepared for the incoming attack, but suddenly—his expression changed when he saw the leading Light Born grin ever so slightly—
Something was wrong.
He realized it, but before he could understand or think about it, the beam the Light Borns had gathered moved. Nux tried to dodge but—
The beam struck Nux directly.
WFFOOOOOOOFFSSHH
The blinding storm instantly overwhelmed his entire body as he vanished into thin air.
The Light Borns’ eyes glinted.
This was one of their trump cards—an attack that could defeat even the beings with the strongest defense—but...
Once again, as the light faded—
They saw him.
Walking forward...throughthe beam as if it did not affect him one bit.
The only thing that was burning and constantly regenerating were his clothes. As for his body...
Nothing.
There was nothing on it.
Even their ’greatest’ attack had failed—utterly.
"N-No! This can’t be!"
One Light Born, losing his sense of control, tried to intercept him, summoning a Sword of Solarity—a blade of energy that could split literal worlds in half.
He swung but...
Tak
Nux caught the sword bare-handed.
Then, he looked into the Light Born’s eyes and—
He used more force.
The divine blade trembled, its light flickering as cracks appeared along its length.
Then—
CRACK
The legendary sword—the relic that almost every being in the Universe who knew about it would covet—shattered into pieces.
The Light Born carrying it stared at Nux in absolute horror, and Nux...
He just extended his hand and grabbed him by his head.
Again, the familiar scene repeated, and in front of all the other Light Borns, another one of their comrades vanished.
Silence.
Absolute silence fell over the place.
The Light Borns stared at the monstrous being in front of them in horror, while Nux continued walking toward them.
By now, it was already clear—
The fight was uneven.
The difference between the two sides was simply too big. Even the Light Borns’ strongest attacks—the ones where they combined all their strength—failed, not even managing to graze the enemy’s skin.
Nux had realized it as well. Even if he wanted to use them as training dummies, they weren’t enough to push him to his limits.
At best, they could only help him get used to his body, and for now, that was all Nux decided to be satisfied with.
"Come on now.
Don’t give in.
Make it more fun, will you?"
He provoked, and his provocation worked.
The Light Borns charged at him; he too grabbed and devoured them one by one, all while dodging their attacks and getting used to the body that now felt foreign to him.

chapters.title: Chapter 2172: This was no longer a battle.
paragraphs: BOOOOM
CLANG
SSHHRRKKKK
The dark void was no longer quiet.
It trembled with every strike, every movement, every breath.
The once endless darkness was now filled with flashes of gold and silver, waves of light clashing against a constant, dark... shadow—shadow that seemed to devour everything it touched.
For hours, the battle had continued.
The Light Borns—the proud, radiant beings who stood at the top of all existence—fought relentlessly, giving their all to resist the enemy in front of them.
But...
But it wasn’t working.
The pride they had for being the Supreme Borns, the pride that was instilled into them, the pride that made them believe they were meant to stand above all...
It was crushed into pieces.
And it didn’t happen in a single moment—it happened slowly, so slowly that even if they wanted to believe all of this was an illusion, that it wasn’t real, they couldn’t.
This was very much real.
Out of the initial hundred and four Light Borns, only about fifty of them were left now.
Others had already been devoured—consumed completely, right in front of them—by the monster who was now floating calmly in the center of the battlefield.
Nux Leander.
The Anomaly.
The being who... even after fighting for hours, did not look tired.
The being who... even after facing a hundred enemies alone, never once looked outnumbered.
The being who... never once looked like he was fighting.
"Keep your distance! Don’t attack alone!"
One of the surviving Light Borns shouted, his golden armor cracked and his wings flickering weakly.
The other Light Borns obeyed automatically—after all, they had done this countless times already—formation after formation, strike after strike, they had tried everything.
And it had all failed.

These were the same beings who had faced countless strong opponents in their long lives, beings who had the power to destroy worlds, beings who commanded armies and terrified even the High Level Worlds,
But...
Nothing—absolutely nothing—had ever felt as hopeless as this.
The enemy moved calmly, almost... lazily.
His breathing was steady, his body no longer jerked awkwardly like before.
Every movement was measured, precise, almost... beautiful.
His strikes no longer broke more than he intended. His steps no longer sent shockwaves by accident.
He was in control. He was still not perfect, but close enough.
He reached out, caught a spear of light midair, and twirled it casually in his hand before snapping it like a twig.
"Enough of this mockery! What do you want from us!?"
A Light Born cried out in frustration, summoning another wave of light sigils around him as he screamed in a voice full of rage and... fear.
Nux glanced at him, his golden eyes showed amusement.
"Want?"
He chuckled softly. There was absolutely no sense of danger in his voice; if anything, he sounded more like this was all a... play.
A stage show meant for amusement, an act where... everything was supposed to go exactly like the script that he already knew.
"I already told you, didn’t I? I’m just... practicing."
He answered, his tone not changing even as he dodged the series of light spears that were aimed at him.
"Practicing!?"
Another Light Born shouted, his wings flaring in rage.
"Do you think this is a game!?"
Nux laughed at that question.
"Everything’s a game.
You just lose faster than others."
"Y-You...!
You bastard!"
One of them charged forward, his sword blazing with intense golden light.
"You dare look down on us!? I’ll show you what happens to—!"
"Yap less,
Just move."
Nux replied, provoking him even further as he signaled him to come at him.
And the Light Born did exactly that—
BOOOOOM
His golden blade struck Nux square in the chest. He didn’t even bother blocking it with an arm.
An explosion covered everything, blinding the Light Born who initiated the attack, but this time, the Light Born grinned.
He felt it!
This time, he felt it for sure!
The attack connected!
This was it! The first time they would be able to draw the enemy’s blood! Or at least... that was what the Light Born thought but...
When the light faded away... just like before...

Nux was still standing, completely unharmed. His clothes were torn a little, but his... body—the sword seemed like it was just resting on his chest, unable to move forward despite the Light Born doing his best.
"I-It can’t be...
I used everything..."
The Light Born stared blankly, his hands trembling as he started questioning his very existence.
But Nux...
He had an entirely different concern.
"It’s good that you’re trying hard, but I have said this before,
Stop using your Life Force to strengthen your attacks. I cannot have you overuse your Life Force and be unusable later.
That will be problematic."
Saying those words, he reached out before the Light Born could retreat. The Light Born tried to dodge, but with Nux now having much better control over his body, it was simply impossible.
Nux’s fingers closed around the Light Born’s head, the familiar black energy seeped out—
"No...! Wait—!"
The Light Born’s words were cut short as the dark energy surrounded him completely and then—
He was gone.
There was no explosion, no fancy tricks, no lights,
Only... silence and darkness—darkness different from the ones the Light Borns were familiar with.
"That was fifty-sixth."
Nux, on the other hand, muttered softly, rubbing his wrist slightly. His tone was so casual that it felt like he was counting the number of push-ups he had done.
The Light Borns around him hesitated, none dared to move, none of them wanted to end up like those who had disappeared.
But... standing still wasn’t going to help them.
The space around Nux warped again—it was a sign, a sign that he was about to move again. A signal he gave out every time he moved, yes—a signal Nux gave out.
A signal he used to alert the enemies, to tell them to be prepared, to tell them... that he was coming.
Yes,
This was no longer a battle.
He was simply toying with them.𝗳𝗿𝐞𝕖𝘄𝗲𝕓𝗻𝚘𝚟𝕖𝐥.𝚌𝕠𝕞

paragraphs: Yes—a signal Nux gave out.
A signal he used to alert the enemies, to tell them to be prepared, to tell them... that he was coming.
Yes,
This was no longer a battle.
He was simply toying with them.
"Be u-unusable later!?
What do you mean!?
What do you want from us!?"
One of the Light Borns shouted desperately as his voice began to crack.
"You are clearly powerful enough to defeat us in one go, then why do you keep doing this!?"
Nux looked at him with a frown—
"Do you people have a recorder inside you or something?
Why do you keep asking the same thing over and over again?
I told you before—
You’re helping me improve."
"Improve...?"
One of them repeated weakly.
"I got stronger too quickly, wasn’t used to my new strength, and I have been using you to deal with it.
Obviously, the pace isn’t exactly according to my standards, but you are currently the best things I have,
So I guess you can say you’ve been... helpful."
Nux nodded, praising them without holding back, but the Light Borns...
They didn’t see this as praise. Their bodies trembled in intense anger. For beings who had once stood at the very top, that single sentence shattered the last of their pride.
"Things...?"
One of them muttered.
"You... you are using us as... toys?"
"You dare treat the Children of Light as your tools!?"
Another snapped.
"Not tools."
Nux defended himself.
"Training dummies.
Let’s keep it accurate."
The Light Borns felt their very bodies collapsing at the ridiculousness and anger they felt.
"YOU VILE... THING!"
They screamed before they all burst forward together, their golden halos blazing strongly.
WHOOSH WHOOSH WHOOSH

Hundreds of radiant spears appeared from all directions—lightstorms, faith bursts, sigil bombardments—every ability these Light Borns had ever mastered, it was all used at the same time without holding back one bit.
The void which was once dark and lightless turned completely gold, and the intensity only continued to increase even further.
But in front of that golden storm...
Nux just grinned, looking forward to what was about to come.
With enraged eyes, the Light Borns lowered their hands, beginning the bombardment, and Nux...
He moved.

And this time, he moved with precision. In this golden storm, he looked like a shadow dancing through sunlight. Every movement was conscious, every step was calculated. His arms moved through the air, redirecting attacks into each other.
One Light Born tried to pierce his back. Nux twisted without looking, catching the attack by the wrist and slamming the attacker into another Light Born, making them both lose their balance.
Another one tried to bind him with a Light Sigil chain, but Nux flicked his fingers—and the chain shattered like glass.
Just like that, the battle continued. Nux continued to dodge everything, for hours.
And the worst part?
Even if he was caught in one of the attacks, it... it simply made no difference.

His body came out unhurt, and the attack didn’t even shift his focus. Even when he was caught in an attack and was ’under its impact,’ he was dodging other attacks, completely ignoring the said ’impact.’
And this sight...
It...
It broke the Light Borns.
The golden beings no longer shouted in unity.
Their movements were mechanical now—they moved just for the sake of moving. There was no intent behind it, their hope...
Their hope had already been crushed.
"What... what sort of monstrosity are you?"
One of them whispered when he got caught. Unlike others, who showed desperation and fear when they were caught, this one seemed... relieved.
Almost as if he needed a reason to stop.
He didn’t even resist when the black energy surrounded him; he... he simply let go.
And when Nux saw it, he stared at the rest of the Light Borns with a deadpan look on his face.
"Come on now, will you?
Show some spirit!"
He spoke as he clenched his fists, as if motivating them not to give up.
"Also, being training dummies isn’t that bad, now is it?
Weren’t you the ones who were disappointed that I didn’t kill the Light Infinity? This is exactly the moment where you can be of help!
Fight me with everything you have, help me improve and who knows? I might just succeed!"
He gave a small motivating speech but...
It clearly wasn’t working.
The Light Borns...
They didn’t even reply. They just moved and switched to another formation as the battle continued further.
By now, Nux’s movements were smooth and effortless.
He could appear anywhere he wished, strike as he intended, control his strength exactly as he imagined.
Of course, there were still times where he misjudged—using too much force, moving too far—but those moments were rare now.
Each mistake he made, he corrected within seconds.
Every time he got caught by one of the attacks, he analyzed, adjusted, and made sure it never happened in a similar manner again.
And every time he improved, the Light Borns broke even further.
They had been fighting for hours, and no, their bodies weren’t tired. These were beings capable of fighting for centuries without needing rest.
A few hours would make no difference to them, but...
But their minds...
Their minds were collapsing.
How could they not?
They were being used as tools—tools this monster was using to sharpen himself. From the beginning till the end, he never once took them seriously.
And why would he?
Even their strongest of attacks only managed to tear his clothes. In these past few hours, not once had they managed to even so much as graze his skin, let alone hurt him.
This...
This was no longer a fight—
It was... humiliation.
An endless cycle where they gave their all, tried new formations, caught the enemy off guard, only for it to end with...
Hopelessness.
"Haaahh..."
After a while, Nux sighed as well.
"Sixty-eighth."
He muttered lazily as he devoured another.
With the number of enemies diminishing and him getting stronger, this was... getting boring, too easy.
The last time he was caught by an attack was three hours ago.
The worst part?
The Light Borns weren’t even trying at this point!
They no longer moved in coordination, they no longer showed anger or frustration, they all had just...
Resigned.
"Whatever, I’ll get what I can from them."
Nux muttered to himself before he began moving.
But then—
’Nux.’
He paused as he heard a familiar voice.
’Something happened.’
Shadow informed.
’What is it?’
He asked.
’It’s the Light Infinity.
Come see for yourself.’
She called. Nux looked at the remaining Light Borns and then—
’Give me a minute.’
He spoke as he then moved.
This time, there was no ’signal,’ something that surprised the Light Borns, but before they could realize what was different—
Nux was already in front of them.

They attacked again, golden beams, swords, and explosions filled the void again, but Nux ignored them completely. Every blast struck him, but his body didn’t even flinch. The light burned around him, but neveronhim.
He reached the first two Light Borns, grabbed them by their heads—one in each hand—and the dark energy exploded outward, swallowing them whole.
Both vanished in an instant.
"W-What—No!"
"Stay away from—!"
The Light Borns stuttered, but they weren’t given time to react. He kept moving—with every few seconds, another pair disappeared.
Two.
Four.
Six.
Eight.
He didn’t even bother dodging now. Attacks hit him, explosions burned around him, but nothing changed. He just kept moving, kept catching, kept devouring.
And in less than a minute, the void was empty.
All Light Borns were devoured.
The ’battle’ was over.

chapters.title: Chapter 2174: We continue what we have been doing.
paragraphs: [The Chain Breakers will be the first step Light takes.
To all life that still breathes within the embrace of the cosmos—
Do not fear the coming storm.
Do not bow to those who claim dominion through shadow.
Because the Light has not yet died.
The Light will shine again—
And this time, it will be brighter than ever.]
Once the sound recording ended, silence fell in Nux’s Universe. Nux stared at his wives, and one look was enough for him to see it—they were shaken.
And why would they not be?
The enemy was an Infinity.
An Infinity—one of the four strongest beings in the entire Universe, beings whose ’awakening’ alone shook the entire Universe.
And it wasn’t just his wives; he too had a solemn look on his face. His eyes slowly turned towards Shadow, who had called him back after this, and—
"...the entire Universe heard this?"
He asked, the disbelief in his voice clear.
It was something that took the women by surprise. It was usually their husband who surprised others, not the other way around—but then again, this wasn’t the ’usual’ time.
The enemy was literally addressing the entire Universe, and this wasn’t done through an artifact or something like that—she did it... on her own.

While they were still figuring out a way to spread their message to the entire Universe, coming up with gimmicks like using blood magic or using artifacts that activated on their own after they destroyed the targeted worlds—

Her voice traveled the entirety of the Universe, reaching every corner of the still-expanding cosmos—even the worlds at the far edge of the Universe, the ones who had never heard or cared about the Anomaly or the Supreme Worlds, heard her.
The distance her voice traveled couldn’t even be calculated; the number wasthathuge.
And she seemed to have done this task they considered impossible... with ease.

Just this alone was more than enough to show the difference between them. Of course, this wasn’t directly linked to their strength—if looked at objectively, this act alone should not have been that intimidating—but...
Even then...
The women and Nux were intimidated.
This was the declaration of war.
It had begun.
All this while, it was only them poking fingers at the enemy, who wasn’t responding, but now, it had changed.
The enemy had responded.
And now...
It was on them to think about how they would react.
Shadow nodded at Nux’s words.
"The slaves we have placed throughout the Universe, they all heard it without exception."
"...how are the people reacting to it?"
Nux asked.

Their actions till now were mostly done to rile up the enemy. Throughout these years, Amaya, together with Melia, Shadow, and Aeliana, had targeted and enslaved billions, positioning them in different worlds spread throughout the Universe.
Yes, the women had created their own little information network—a network no being would ever be able to discover, since the ones who were part of that very network had no clue they were in it.
Their only role was to live without knowing anything; it was the women who constantly checked their memories to get the answers they wanted.
This was what Nux had been using to learn of the general direction people’s hearts were in.
The confusion that spread when the Reaper’s Veil disappeared and the Supreme Worlds called for all mercenary worlds—
The amusement when some unknown group tried to challenge the Supreme Worlds—
The panic when the same unknown group took a bigger action and destroyed High-Level Worlds—

Nux knew about it all through them. No, more precisely, all of this happened in the said sequence because Nux knew the general sentiment and manipulated it accordingly—in a way that would help him achieve his goal.
Infighting between the Four Supreme Factions.
Even now, his next action would depend on how the people reacted, and Shadow, who knew that, had prepared the answer accordingly—
"Most are relieved. Even though this was the first time most had heard of the existence called Seraphielle Light, the voice in itself carried an unshakable confidence and sense of ease.
And since the name ’Supreme World of Light’ already holds so much power, influencing people wasn’t a difficult task for her.
But..."
"But?"
Nux raised his eyebrow, waiting for the good news.
And Shadow didn’t disappoint.
"While many feel the matter will be solved since the strongest being in existence has taken charge, some feel... uneasy."
"Scared?"
Nux grinned, and Shadow nodded.
"They fear retaliation.
They fear that this might lead to something bigger—something they will be dragged into as well."
"That’s a logical conclusion."
Nux nodded to himself.
This was what he was aiming for from the beginning. The more uneasy people were, the less they would believe in the Supreme Worlds.
What surprised him was that only a few reacted the way he wanted them to.
"It is logical, yes.
But most of the time, logic isn’t what drives people—especially the en masse."
Amaya spoke up.
"In a situation like this, most will only see that an Infinity, the strongest being in the Universe, has taken action, so the matter will naturally be concluded in time.
But—
What their minds will conveniently overlook is the fact that from the beginning, the ’enemy’ was trying to provoke the said being to take action.
If anything, everything was going exactly like the enemy wanted it to—so instead of rejoicing, they should be... worried.
Because if the enemy had a plan—and the said plan is now one step closer to completion—this, in no way, is good news for any of them."
The devourer spoke.
Nux nodded at her words, then he just shrugged—
"Maybe this is their mind’s way of easing their lives."
He commented.
"It’s not like being aware would help them in any way. After all, in the grand scheme of things...
They are... insignificant."
"If they were all aware, it could have made a difference."
Aeliana commented, but—
"They are too weak to do anything. If anything, they would have been a crowd that’s harder to manipulate."
Nux didn’t care.
He just glanced at his wives and—
"So? What’s next?
What do we do now?"
"Get more people on our side."
Amaya had already prepared the answer.
"Too many people feel at ease right now. If this continues, they will be influenced by Light and strengthen Seraphielle—we cannot allow that to happen.
Uncertainty, uneasiness, panic—
We need it all.
And to do this—
We continue what we have been doing.
It is time we move the immortal army."

At Amaya’s words, Nux turned his head, and his eyes fell on around two hundred and fifty Eternals, all hovering in the void with their eyes closed.
This was... their ’harvest’.
The result of everything they had been doing so far.
Yes, in the past few days, Nux hadn’t just devoured worlds, he... he had devoured beings too.
Beings who were closest to the Universe right after the Four Infinities, beings who would otherwise have the power to make literal worlds move with just their words alone.
But right now—
More than two hundred and fifty such beings were hovering right in front of them.
"It’s quite a grand collection."
Vyriana commented with a chuckle.
"One hundred and ten Light Borns, one Eternity Born, one Darkness Born, and more than a hundred and fifty other Eternals—
This is more than enough to crush any High-Level World into pieces within mere seconds, a hundred times over."
Astaria nodded as well, analyzing everything.
"And all of this is when we aren’t even counting other beings we have devoured so far."
Shadow added, looking in another direction where more than ten thousand beings remained unconscious—these were the beings who weren’t Eternals.
Most of them were Transcendents; there were even some Primordials and a few Sovereigns.
"They do not matter."
Riona shook her head.
"At least not right now."
They were only targeting High-Level Worlds, and while some of these beings were good enough to be troublesome even to High-Level Worlds, in the bigger picture, they weren’t as important.
They were mostly there to fill in the numbers or to expand their attacks further when they began to target Lower-Level Worlds again.
"With the addition of a hundred of these..."
Thyra began, staring at the hundred Light Borns,
"...I guess our attacks will be much more well-coordinated, huh?"
"Do we finally move to the final part then?"
Rune asked.
"This is the best time, yes."
Felberta nodded.𝙛𝒓𝓮𝙚𝔀𝒆𝒃𝓷𝒐𝓿𝙚𝓵.𝙘𝒐𝒎

"Alright then."

The moment her golden eyes fell on him, the being made of light flinched and lowered his head even further.
"Report."
She commanded, and Lord Light obeyed.
"What have we lost?"
Seraphielle asked.
"We have lost..."
The reporting began.
Lord Light told everything—every world, every being, everything that belonged to the Light Faction and was now lost. Everything was reported.

The patterns in which the attacks began, the time it took for the enemy to move from one world to another—every little detail, every single thing that the Light Borns who had been investigating the matter for the past few hours had gathered—everything was reported in a well-structured manner.

The report mentioned how it all began when the mercenaries were gathered, then what happened at Gracevale, the other High-Level Worlds that were targeted one after another, until finally, the few worlds that were targeted all at the same time—
"So what began as a one-man show has now turned into... the work of an army?"
Seraphielle asked, raising an eyebrow. The frown that appeared on her divine face was... a sight to see—something even Lord Light hadn’t seen in a long, long while.
"Yes."
Lord Light nodded.

Then, with a wave of his hand, the inscriptions in the temple moved, and a light screen began hovering in the air, showing the records of Light Borns facing the said army before the vision was cut off.
Seraphielle frowned at that, but soon, the recording went back and zoomed in on one of the enemies the Light Borns were facing—someone even Seraphielle recognized.
"This is..."
"Silvaris Gracevale."
Lord Light answered.
"One of the Fifteen Gracevale Eternals who is said to have disappeared."
Seraphielle narrowed her eyes at those words.
"The enemy doesn’t just ’disappear’ together with its preys, he... recruits them."
Lord Light explained.
"At first, I did not believe it.
What could possibly make beings, especially Eternals who know of your existence, turn against you?
I believed that the enemy took over their minds and changed who they are, and I still believe it to some extent, but...
After merging with your alternative consciousness... I have another theory."
Seraphielle looked at him, signaling him to continue, and that was what he did.
"When the enemy ’disappears’ with the preys, he takes them to the Universe he came from. There, they see his strength, and maybe...
Maybe that is what gives them the bravery to... betray us."

Lord Light mentioned with slight hesitation, but since he too, together with Seraphielle, had merged with the alternate consciousness that conversed with other Infinities and came up with the theory of all this being the beginning of an invasion from another Universe, he knew he had to mention it.
And Seraphielle...
She didn’t strongly react to his words either. Just as Lord Light thought, she too had expected it to some extent.
"What else do you know?"
She asked calmly, wanting to sort everything before taking the next action.
But...
Her question was only met with silence.
She glanced at her creation, only to see him lowering his head in embarrassment, and Seraphielle found the answer to her question.
Nothing.
They did not know anything else.
Lord Light trembled, fearing what Seraphielle might do next, but...
"Gather more information."
Seraphielle just ordered calmly.
An act that surprised Lord Light—a second chance!
He was given a second chance!
However, before he could rejoice and kowtow in gratitude,
[L-Lady Seraphielle!]
A desperate voice was heard.
And it didn’t come from just one being—
As Seraphielle and Lord Light turned towards the Orb of Resonance, they saw more than thirty stars shining brightly—all of them were trying to contact them at the same time—
[[[Ara#@$$ is being attacked!]]]
The voices were overlapped, but both Seraphielle and Lord Light realized what was happening...
Another attack.
And this time—
Ten High-Level Worlds were being attacked at the same time!
And to think this was happening right after Seraphielle addressed the entire Universe...
This...
This wasn’t just an attack.
It was a statement—
A statement that the enemy too, was ready.

chapters.title: Chapter 2176: Heaven’s Reward.
paragraphs: [[[Ara#@$$ is being attacked!]]]
The voices were overlapped, but both Seraphielle and Lord Light realized what was happening...
Another attack.
And this time—
Ten High-Level Worlds were being attacked at the same time!
"What...?"
Lord Light blinked as he slowly turned toward Seraphielle.
The Light Infinity stared at the Orb; there was no change in her expression, but Lord Light knew...
Seraphielle Light was enraged.
The enemy was openly challenging them.
In an instant, Lord Light knew—they were done for.
For a moment, Seraphielle closed her eyes, connecting her vision with all of the Light Borns at the same time.
Yes, she was using Lord Light’s ability, or more accurately, it was her ability that she had bestowed onto Lord Light.
Within a second, Seraphielle watched and analyzed everything that happened, and then—she turned toward Lord Light.
"The Anomaly doesn’t recruit."
She spoke in a low voice.
"He brainwashes its preys."
"...what?"
Lord Light frowned.
How did she suddenly find it out...?
He wondered in his head, and as if knowing exactly what he was thinking—Seraphielle waved her hand, activating Lord Light’s ability on her own as he saw one of the Light Born’s visions.
That was when he finally saw it—
The Anomaly’s army.
The army that, together with other Eternals... also had... Supreme Borns.
"H-He recruited them.
He recruited Light Borns!"
Lord Light shouted, unable to believe the absurdity of the situation.
Recruiting others by showing their might—that Lord Light could believe—but...
The Light Borns...?
Making it so they willingly betrayed Seraphielle and joined their strength was... impossible.

And it wasn’t about strength. The enemy could be as strong as they wanted—even if the enemy had all other Supreme Worlds by their side, the Light Borns would never join them—or more precisely—theycouldn’tjoin them.

The connection Light Borns had with the Orb of Resonance wasn’t just about communication or sharing vision—the Orb of Resonance held complete control over the Light Borns. As long as the connection existed, be it killing them with a mere thought or even altering their memories and turning them into puppets—it was possible.
But—
"T-The connection..."
Lord Light, who returned to the temple, stuttered, his body flickering, unable to believe what he was seeing.
"The connection disappeared!"
He spoke, staring at Seraphielle in disbelief.
This was the connection every Light Born was born with! It was part of them! They simply could not survive without it!
This very connection gave meaning to their existence; without it, they were just anchorless beings who did not belong anywhere—
Suddenly, Lord Light’s expression changed.
He continued to stare at Seraphielle, and very quickly, he realized that she realized it as well.
"They... became a part of their Universe... giving them a new meaning to their existence."
Seraphielle didn’t say anything; her eyes still did not reflect any emotions. She had already concluded all this with just a mere gaze.
Right now—
She was coming up with a counterplan.
The enemy had changed their tactics. Before, the enemy still needed time to attack a world, force its Will to come out, and devour it.
But now...
Now the enemy wasn’t waiting—they no longer cared about devouring the World’s Will.
They only had one goal—destruction.
And when an army of more than ten Eternals—with the Supreme Borns leading them—attacked, no High-Level World would be able to survive for more than a minute without reinforcements.
Even the Universe itself wouldn’t react to a particular world’s destruction since the enemy was no longer ’taking it away’.
So now, Seraphielle was on her own.
But it didn’t matter—
"Move."
The Infinity of Light ordered as a faint pulse of gold spread from her body.
Irethol, a High-Level World, floated like a glowing reef in the dark void. Its surface shimmered in waves of azure and silver, dotted with mountain-sized corals that pulsed with light.
The beings who lived here were called the Thal’ren.

Thal’ren had tall, slender bodies that shined with faint translucent light; their skin was like living glass filled with veins of light. Every Thal’ren had a crest of crystal fins running down their back, and their eyes shifted color with their emotions.
From time immemorial, Irethol was part of the Light Faction—it was one of the key worlds that held a significant amount of influence in the Faction and throughout the Universe.
Even right now, its people were quite busy, constantly coordinating with the Light Borns and keeping an eye out for the enemy. And now that Seraphielle was awake, things had gotten even more hectic.
After the fall of Gracevale, the Lower-Level Worlds that belonged to the Light Faction constantly contacted Irethol, seeking shelter and reassurance.

The Thal’rens were overwhelmed with work—constantly answering hundreds of thousands of lower-level worlds was by no means an easy task, especially when they did not have an already established system to deal with such matters like Gracevale had.
The entirety of Irethol’s work system was close to collapsing since the world couldn’t be divided, but the only thing holding it all together was... the Progenitors’ greed.
The five Irethol Progenitors had a clear plan.
Before it all began, while Irethol was an important member of the Light Faction, its value was still less when compared to Gracevale.
Now, however, things were different.
Gracevale had fallen. Even though it still existed, with its progenitors gone, the world was abandoned—it was only a matter of time before it was attacked and fell completely.
And it wasn’t just Gracevale; a few other ’competitors’ had disappeared as well. Thus—all the responsibility had fallen onto their shoulders, and if they managed to hold on...
This...
This responsibility might permanently become their own, instantly elevating their status in the Faction, giving them power and glory.
They...
They might become the new Gracevale—or better, they might reach a level even Gracevale could not reach.
This was the Irethol Progenitors’ plan, even if it meant overworking their people beyond reason for a while—
Yes, they were working hard and...
The Heavens decided to reward their efforts.

chapters.title: Chapter 2177: They are of Light and we must greet them properly.
paragraphs: This was the Irethol Progenitors’ plan, even if it meant overworking their people beyond reason for a while—
Yes, they were working hard and...
The Heavens decided to reward their efforts.
SWOOOSH
Suddenly, a streak of gold tore through the sky.
Then another.
Another.
And then four more times—
Irethol’s sky parted as seven radiant figures descended, their halos cutting through the storm clouds that had formed from the sheer force of their presence.
Behind them were eleven others—each releasing an aura far stronger than what mere subordinates should have.
Eternals.
All eleven of them were Eternals.
Combined with the seven Light Borns, a total of eighteen Eternals had descended onto Irethol. Their combined aura shook everything around them and painted the entire sky gold.
The Thal’ren people who noticed the sudden change stopped mid-work, looking up from their floating cities with awe and confusion.

Yes, Irethol was a High-Level World, an important member of the Light Faction, but most people in Irethol hadn’t seen Light Borns in their entire lives. It was said that seeing even one Light Born was a once-in-a-million-years miracle, a rare occurrence—but now...
Now seven of them had descended at once.
Were the Progenitors truly correct?
Was this truly the day they would leave the shadows of Gracevale and other worlds? Were they... going to advance and become something far more than a simple High-Level World?
The people’s eyes were filled with hope, their faces reflecting the golden light that these beings released.

And it wasn’t just the common people—in the main coral citadel, five Irethol Progenitors gathered quickly, every single one of them was an Eternal—an absolute being whom no one in the entirety of Irethol could go against.
But right now—these weren’t the absolute beings who demanded absolute loyalty wherever they went—
Right now, these five beings stared at the sky, their eyes shining with greed. If they weren’t conscious of their image, one might even see them rubbing their hands together in glee.
But...
While they were gleeful, yes, something... something did not make sense.
"Irethol’s Will did not react to their arrival."
One of the five Progenitors, a silver-eyed Thal’ren named Zal’ith, commented with a frown, and in an instant, the other Progenitors froze.
...what?
They blinked, and for a moment, their minds did not register it.
But soon, it did.
The Light Borns and other Eternals were hovering right in front of them, their lot was planning on going and greeting them but...
How was it that even when eighteen foreign entities came to their world, their World’s Will did not inform them...?
Just...
Just what was happening?
Another one of the Progenitors, Elyra, connected with the World’s Will and extended her senses—and the moment she did—her frown deepened.
"Irethol’s Will... it is unable to sense them at all...
According to Irethol... these eighteen beings... do not exist."
She muttered.
The rest of the Progenitors did what she did and came to the same conclusion—a conclusion that confused and horrified them at the same time.
"But... how is this possible...?"
Varon, another one of the Progenitors, questioned, his usually deep voice currently shaken.
"Is... is this a relic?"
Zal’ith muttered as he tilted his head.

All other Progenitors turned toward him with flat looks on their faces. Every single one of them knew that a relic capable of hiding an entity from a World’s Will did not exist. If it did, it would have changed the very way Universal Wars worked—
Methods like assassinations, abduction, and other cowardly tactics would become commonplace. Real wars would become secondary, and these tactics would decide the true outcome.
It would be... chaotic.
But...
The other Progenitors knew that Zal’ith knew this as well—plus, they were literallyseeingthe so-called impossible happening in front of their very eyes.
Not to mention...
Wasn’t the Universe already chaotic enough?
Weren’t things that had never happened before in trillions and trillions of years happening one after another as if they were nothing?
What if the Light Faction found a way to create such a relic? What was stopping them from breaking the rules that hadn’t been broken ever before?
When the Progenitors thought about it—
It all made sense.
If anyone could do it, it would be the Supreme Faction.
And didn’t Lady Seraphielle wake up just a few moments ago? What if the relic was a gift she bestowed upon her people?
The moment that thought appeared in their heads, the Progenitors believed it.
Not to mention—
"It does not matter."
Elyra spoke, her expression changing.
"Whether it is a relic, an artifact, or an ability, none of it matters.
They are of Light, and they have come to visit us,
And we must greet them properly."
She declared, her words gaining nods of approval from the other Progenitors.
"Then let us go."

Varon nodded again, and together, the five Eternals emerged from the coral citadel, their bodies rising through the silver waters, breaking through the glimmering surface until they hovered beneath the radiant sky.
The seven Light Borns waited for them—seven beings filled with absolute grace and glowing with golden brilliance.
Both the Light Borns and the beings behind them were Eternals, but despite that... in the eyes of the Irethol Progenitors, the eleven Eternals... simply did not exist.
Varon, the representative of the Irethol Progenitors, stepped out with a pleasing smile and bowed respectfully—
"Honored emissaries of Light,"
He began politely as he then started introducing himself.
"I am Varon Tideflare, one of the five Eternals of Irethol. You honor our world with your—"
But before he could even complete the sentence he had prepared in his mind for the last few seconds—
Pierce
His body jerked as suddenly—
A golden spear burst through his chest.
For a second, the world froze.
Varon looked down slowly, his eyes filled with absolute disbelief.

The spear of light flickered once before turning into liquid that prevented any form of healing. Varon’s luminous blood flowed out without stopping; the golden liquid continued to drain his life force and shut down his vital organs.
"V-Varon...?"
Elyra blinked... unable to believe what was happening.
She wanted to move forward—but before she could, another Light Born raised his hand, and a wall of light formed, cutting her off.
Varon’s body twitched once, then... it went still.
The glow faded from his veins and he...
He fell.
His crystalline body free-falling into the sea below.

Were the Progenitors truly correct?
Was this truly the day they would leave the shadows of Gracevale and other worlds?
Were they... going to advance and become something far more than a simple High-Level World?
The people’s eyes were filled with hope, their faces reflecting the golden light that these beings released.

And it wasn’t just the common people—in the main coral citadel, five Irethol Progenitors gathered quickly, every single one of them was an Eternal—an absolute being whom no one in the entirety of Irethol could go against.
But right now—these weren’t the absolute beings who demanded absolute loyalty wherever they went—
Right now, these five beings stared at the sky, their eyes shining with greed.
If they weren’t conscious of their image, one might even see them rubbing their hands together in glee.
But...
While they were gleeful, yes, something... something did not make sense.
"Irethol’s Will did not react to their arrival."
One of the five Progenitors, a silver-eyed Thal’ren named Zal’ith, commented with a frown, and in an instant, the other Progenitors froze.
...what?
They blinked, and for a moment, their minds did not register it.
But soon, it did.
The Light Borns and other Eternals were hovering right in front of them, their lot was planning on going and greeting them but...
How was it that even when eighteen foreign entities came to their world, their World’s Will did not inform them...?
Just...
Just what was happening?
Another one of the Progenitors, Elyra, connected with the World’s Will and extended her senses—and the moment she did—her frown deepened.
"Irethol’s Will... it is unable to sense them at all...
According to Irethol... these eighteen beings... do not exist."
She muttered.
The rest of the Progenitors did what she did and came to the same conclusion—a conclusion that confused and horrified them at the same time.
"But... how is this possible...?"
Varon, another one of the Progenitors, questioned, his usually deep voice currently shaken.
"Is... is this a relic?"
Zal’ith muttered as he tilted his head.
All other Progenitors turned toward him with flat looks on their faces.
Every single one of them knew that a relic capable of hiding an entity from a World’s Will did not exist.
If it did, it would have changed the very way Universal Wars worked—
Methods like assassinations, abduction, and other cowardly tactics would become commonplace.
Real wars would become secondary, and these tactics would decide the true outcome.
It would be... chaotic.
But...
The other Progenitors knew that Zal’ith knew this as well—plus, they were literallyseeingthe so-called impossible happening in front of their very eyes.
Not to mention...
Wasn’t the Universe already chaotic enough?
Weren’t things that had never happened before in trillions and trillions of years happening one after another as if they were nothing?
What if the Light Faction found a way to create such a relic?
What was stopping them from breaking the rules that hadn’t been broken ever before?
When the Progenitors thought about it—
It all made sense.
If anyone could do it, it would be the Supreme Faction.
And didn’t Lady Seraphielle wake up just a few moments ago?
What if the relic was a gift she bestowed upon her people?
The moment that thought appeared in their heads, the Progenitors believed it.
Not to mention—
"It does not matter."
Elyra spoke, her expression changing.
"Whether it is a relic, an artifact, or an ability, none of it matters.
They are of Light, and they have come to visit us,
And we must greet them properly."
She declared, her words gaining nods of approval from the other Progenitors.
"Then let us go."

Varon nodded again, and together, the five Eternals emerged from the coral citadel, their bodies rising through the silver waters, breaking through the glimmering surface until they hovered beneath the radiant sky.
The seven Light Borns waited for them—seven beings filled with absolute grace and glowing with golden brilliance.
Both the Light Borns and the beings behind them were Eternals, but despite that... in the eyes of the Irethol Progenitors, the eleven Eternals... simply did not exist.
Varon, the representative of the Irethol Progenitors, stepped out with a pleasing smile and bowed respectfully—
"Honored emissaries of Light,"
He began politely as he then started introducing himself.
"I am Varon Tideflare, one of the five Eternals of Irethol.
You honor our world with your—"
But before he could even complete the sentence he had prepared in his mind for the last few seconds—
Pierce
His body jerked as suddenly—
A golden spear burst through his chest.
For a second, the world froze.
Varon looked down slowly, his eyes filled with absolute disbelief.
The spear of light flickered once before turning into liquid that prevented any form of healing.
Varon’s luminous blood flowed out without stopping; the golden liquid continued to drain his life force and shut down his vital organs.
"V-Varon...?"
Elyra blinked... unable to believe what was happening.
She wanted to move forward—but before she could, another Light Born raised his hand, and a wall of light formed, cutting her off.
Varon’s body twitched once, then... it went still.
The glow faded from his veins and he...
He fell.
His crystalline body free-falling into the sea below.

chapters.title: Chapter 2178: WHAT HAVE YOU BECOME!?
paragraphs: "V-Varon...?"

Elyra blinked, unable to believe what had just happened. Her body reacted on its own as she dashed forward—or so she tried to—but another Light Born raised his hand, and a Wall of Light formed in front of her, cutting her off.
By the time she managed to move past the wall and tried to reach Varon again—
It was already too late.
"Acckk! Why... khrrrkk!!"
Varon’s body twitched once, then... it went still. The golden liquid on his wound ate away his endless life force, destroying him from within.
The glow in his veins faded, his eyes lost their shine, and, unable to hold on any longer—
His body fell.
Free falling into the sea below with aplop.
And above the skies, where the Light Borns, the other Eternals following them, and now four Progenitors of Irethol stood... silence fell.
The Progenitors stared at the absurd situation in front of them, frozen. No matter how desperately they tried—
Their bodies just wouldn’t move.
And only after Elyra forced herself to speak did she manage to ask the question all four Progenitors had in their minds.
All of them were from Light—then how... why would the Light Borns... kill one of them...?
Was this a test?
An order from Lady Seraphielle?
What was it?
And why?
But the Light Borns didn’t answer. Instead—
Pierce
Another Light Born had moved, his spear piercing through one of the Thal’ren Eternals—or at least...

That was what happened at first glance, but this time, the Thal’ren Progenitors were prepared. The Progenitor who was attacked, Raphal, moved through the spear that had pierced through his body as if his body were made of jelly, and when he was finally away, his body returned to normal—as if nothing had happened.
The Light Born who attacked Raphal narrowed his eyes, but this didn’t stop him—he moved forward, but just then—
"WHAT ARE YOU DOING!?"
Elyra screamed, her eyes reflecting intense anger.
"WE ARE OF LIGHT!!
WE ARE ONE OF YOU!!!
WHY ARE YOU ATTACKING US!?"
She demanded to know as she too took out her weapon, prepared for whatever was about to come.
And just then—as if just holding her weapon was enough for her to collect herself—
Her very demeanour changed.
"If we do not receive proper explanation, do not blame us for being rude."
She spoke calmly, her eyes shining with strong conviction. Her words also brought the other Progenitors out of their reverie; they too brought out their weapons and stared at the Light Borns.

Yes, they were of Light; they followed the Supreme World of Light, and in their eyes, the Light Borns were no different than messengers of Lady Seraphielle herself, beings they deeply respected—but...
But this did not mean they did not have pride of their own.
These beings came totheirworld and killed one of their own. This was not a greeting, this was... a direct assault, and if they thought they could get away with it, they were sorely mistaken.
Light Borns or not, it didn’t even matter that they held the numbers advantage—the Irethol Progenitors just couldn’t give in.

And it wasn’t just them; the rest of the Thal’rens, who saw everything happen right in front of their eyes, stared at the situation wide-eyed, but following their Progenitors, their shock too had turned into anger.
But...
To the Light Borns—their resistance simply did not matter.
The leading Light Born, Farah, raised his hand, attracting all attention. The Irethol Progenitors stared at him, waiting for an answer—
But no answer came.
What came was—
Farah’s gaze swept over them without even the slightest change in his expression, and then—
Then he flicked his hand.
The six Light Borns and eleven other Eternals behind him moved as one, targeting the four Irethol Progenitors.
Their answer was clear.
Battle was the only way out.
And when the Irethol Progenitors realized it—
They moved forward as well.
BOOOOOOOM
The sky of Irethol split apart.
Golden and silver light collided, scattering waves of wild energy that tore through the sea and sky alike.
The calm, radiant world that was shining with serenity just a few minutes ago had now turned into a complete, chaotic mess.
Elyra darted through the air, her crystal fins blazing with light as she parried a spear aimed at her throat.
"STOP THIS MADNESS!"
She shouted, her voice echoing through the trembling skies.
"WE ARE OF LIGHT! WHY ARE YOU DOING THIS!?"
But no one answered.
The six Light Borns moved together, their coordination so perfect that the Irethol Progenitors couldn’t find even a single flaw in it.
Every strike they made rippled with perfect brilliance, their bodies shifting through light itself as they moved.
They weren’t like other beings; they... they seemed to represent inevitability itself.

Behind them, the eleven Eternals launched their attacks as well. They too were all part of the Light Faction, so their energies were somewhat related to light. Their radiance, though incomparable to the Light Borns, was still something the Irethol Progenitors simply could not ignore.
"Formation!"
Zal’ith, one of the Irethol Progenitors, shouted.
He and the other three Progenitors moved into a tight circle, their bodies surrounded by runes made of ocean light.
"Shield of the Depth!"

The waters of Irethol surged upward, forming a colossal dome that shimmered around them. By now, Irethol’s Will was activated as well. It had already lost one of its children, so it gave all its power to its remaining children.

This was also the reason the Light Borns couldn’t suppress them with their domains—both sides had absolute laws. Even though the Light Borns’ Laws were stronger, the Irethol Progenitors had the support of a High-Level World.
So the battle wasn’t entirely hopeless.
Or at least...
That is what the Irethol Progenitors believed.
But...
One Light Born, Alvian, raised his hand. He looked at the dome in front of him without emotion, then, for the first time since the Light Borns had arrived,
One of them spoke.
"Shatter."

He commanded, and the ocean barrier the Irethol Progenitors had created together—a barrier stronger than any they had made before, a miles-wide shield reinforced by the Will of Irethol—shattered instantly.
BOOOOOOM
The explosion sent the four Progenitors flying backward.
Zal’ith crashed into the coral spires below, sending waves of broken glass and glowing shards scattering into the sea.
Raphal roared, summoning pillars of light from the ocean floor, striking upward—but every beam he sent was casually redirected by one of the corrupted Eternals.
BOOM BOOM BOOM
The battlefield became even more chaotic.

Each attack from the Light Borns destroyed everything it touched. Mountains of coral disintegrated into glowing dust, the sea turned into steam, and every city below them screamed in panic, their cries lost under the thunder of godly beings clashing.
Elyra, breathing heavily, turned toward Raphal.
"Raphal, flank right! Zal’ith—!"
But her command broke off when she saw it—
A golden spear pierced straight through Raphal’s back.
He froze mid-flight, his body trembling as his veins lit up like rivers of molten gold.
"E-Elyra..."
He called out, his words losing strength with time.
Then—
BOOOM
His body exploded into dust.
"NO!"
Elyra screamed, but before she could even process the sight—
BOOOOOOOOOM𝒇𝓻𝓮𝓮𝙬𝙚𝒃𝒏𝓸𝙫𝒆𝙡.𝓬𝓸𝒎
Another blast came from above.
The light struck Zal’ith squarely, vaporizing the entire stretch of ocean beneath him, together with him.
Yes, Zal’ith had fallen as well.
The battlefield was falling apart.
Their resistance... it barely lasted a minute.
Elyra and the last Progenitor regrouped mid-air, battered and bloodied, their breaths harsh and shallow.
"Th-They’re monsters..."
Krayn, the one remaining Progenitor, muttered, his once radiant fins now broken and dull.
"One of them could destroy us all.
Why... why are they doing this!?"
"Focus!"
Elyra shouted, clutching her bleeding arm.
"We’ll make them hear us! They have to!"
She raised her hand, channeling her essence into the air.
A giant wave of light burst outward—an ancient Thal’ren technique meant to prepare one final attack, an attack that even the Light Borns wouldn’t be able to ignore.
But—
SWHOOOSH
Before the call could finish, a beam of light cut through the wave, erasing it completely.
"It is pointless.
Accept your end—
It is inevitable."
The Light Born who destroyed it looked at her with calm eyes.
But—
"You kill your own and you dare talk about inevitability!?"
Elyra shouted back, her voice filled with fury and... despair.
"WHAT HAVE YOU BECOME!?"
She asked, her voice shaking the entirety of Irethol.
But...
No response came.
The six Light Borns advanced again, moving like angels of judgment. Their light engulfed everything—the sky, the ocean, even the cries of the dying.
"I WILL TAKE ONE OF YOU DOWN WITH ME!!"
Krayn screamed and launched his final attack, releasing all his life force into one strike.
A giant serpent of golden light formed and charged at one of the Light Borns.
It reached him...
And...
Then it simply vanished the moment it touched the Light Borns’ combined radiance.
As for Krayn...
His body instantly turned cold, his light faded, and...
He fell—just like Varon, Raphal, and Zal’ith.
Elyra was the last one left.
